components.text: Sign in to the DigitalOcean account or team you want to connect.

Open Applications & API and generate a personal access token. Choose a name and expiration. In Custom Scopes, enable account:read for the connection check, then add only permissions needed by your tasks. Copy the generated token into the field below.

Choose your Ragentic workspace and connection name. Test reads your account UUID without changing resources. A successful test only proves access to /v2/account; other operations need their own scopes and resource identifiers. Save stores an encrypted credential and connector. Copy or download the one-time export. To rotate or revoke a token, update it in DigitalOcean, then replace the saved Ragentic credential from Manage credentials and test the connection again.

console_upgrade.description: The connection is upgraded to a WebSocket. Binary frames from the client are terminal input, and text frames are resize messages such as `{"resize":{"rows":40,"cols":120}}`. Binary frames from the server are terminal output with `stdout` and `stderr` combined. Text frames from the server are control messages: `{"status":{"state":"resuming"}}` while a paused MicroVM resumes, `{"error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}}` when the console fails to connect or start (with `code` set to `dial_failed`, `start_failed`, or `agent_error`), and `{"exit":{"code":0}}` when the shell exits. The server sends a ping every 30 seconds. A console closes after 4 hours, or after 30 minutes with no input and no output. A message larger than 1 MiB closes the console with WebSocket code 1009.

agent_config.description: Immutable team-scoped Environment Config: one sanitized manifest per config. There is no update; clone to a new config to change content.

agentspec_schema_version.description: The manifest contract the server accepted at create time: the manifest's own apiVersion for legacy envelope parses (currently agents.digitalocean.com/v1alpha1), or agents.digitalocean.com/flat.v1 for flat-format parses.

content_hash.description: Lowercase SHA-256 hex digest of the canonical sanitized manifest JSON.

created_by.description: Authenticated user identity that created the config.

credentials.description: Redacted credential slot metadata (name/source/provider). Secret values are never included.

allOf.description: The per-signal telemetry opt-in recorded at create time. Absent when the customer expressed no choice. This echoes the create-time request only: a customer who later re-toggles a signal from the Insights settings page changes their enablement there, not here.

manifest.description: Canonical runnable environment spec JSON, immutable after create. Validated non-secret spec.env and spec.permissions remain; spec.secrets retains name/source/provider but omits ref and the write-only value; metadata.name is cleared while safe metadata such as labels remains.

agent_config_clone_request.description: Clone body: required new name plus write-only credentials for any declared slots. No lineage field.

name.description: New config name, unique among the team's active configs.

oauth_assignments.description: Write-only map from oauth logical slot to an OAuth assignment UUID. Required when the source declares those slots; never copied from the source.

secrets.description: Write-only map from tenantSecret logical slot to plaintext. Required when the source declares those slots; never copied from the source.

agent_config_create_request.description: Environment Config create body. Credentials are not request fields: every secret is declared in the environment spec under secrets (or legacy spec.secrets), with tenantSecret slots carrying plaintext in a write-only value extracted into Secrets Manager and never returned.

allOf.description: Optional per-signal Insights telemetry opt-in. Travels beside manifest_yaml, never inside it: the manifest is immutable and content-hashed, while this value can be changed later from the Insights settings page. When omitted, no choice is recorded and the product default applies.

manifest_yaml.description: Customer environment-spec YAML text. The HTTP JSON body is capped at 1 MiB and this field is capped at 512 KiB.
manifest_yaml.example:
apiVersion: agents.digitalocean.com/v1alpha1
kind: Agent
spec:
  runtime:
    adapter: opencode

name.description: Config name, case-insensitively unique among the team's active configs.

agent_config_summary.description: Lightweight list representation; the manifest is available from config reads, not list responses.

agentspec_schema_version.description: The manifest contract the server accepted at create time: the manifest's own apiVersion for legacy envelope parses (currently agents.digitalocean.com/v1alpha1), or agents.digitalocean.com/flat.v1 for flat-format parses.

content_hash.description: Lowercase SHA-256 hex digest of the canonical sanitized manifest JSON.

created_by.description: Authenticated user identity that created the config.

agent_consent.description: Consent details for a specific environment.

agent_id.description: The unique identifier of the environment. For Harness Runtime, this is the Environment Config ID.

enabled.description: Whether signals collection is enabled for this environment.

environment_id.description: Same as agent_id. Dual-emitted during the rename.

id.description: The unique numeric identifier for the consent record.

source.description: The source this consent applies to. Always `agent` for per-environment records returned by this endpoint.

team_id.description: The team ID that owns this consent record.

updated_at.description: A time value given in ISO8601 combined date and time format.

agent_kind.description: AgentKind identifies what runs inside the session sandbox. CreateSession accepts CLAUDE_CODE, OPENCODE, CODEX_CLI, CURSOR_CLI, OPENAI_CODEX, LANGGRAPH, and CREWAI (the supported set is overridable via HARNESS_SUPPORTED_AGENT_KINDS); other values are rejected with 400. AGENT_KIND_OPENAI_CODEX is the OpenAI sandbox-provider kind (DO runs codex exec-server; the agent loop lives at OpenAI). AGENT_KIND_LANGGRAPH is the LangGraph framework adapter. AGENT_KIND_CREWAI is the CrewAI Crew framework adapter: like LANGGRAPH the template bakes no agent code, so spec.env must supply FRAMEWORK_REPO and FRAMEWORK_REPO_SHA; a Crew kickoff is one-shot and exposes no HITL surface. CREWAI is additionally gated per team and returns 400 for teams it is not enabled for.

agent_manifest.description: Customer-authored agents.yaml Agent manifest, sent as the CreateSession request body with a YAML Content-Type. Two formats are accepted during the dual-format transition: the FLAT format (primary - no envelope, snake_case, duration strings; authoritative published schema contracts/agent.flat.schema.json, field reference docs/agent-manifest.md) and the legacy v1alpha1 envelope documented by the properties below (DEPRECATED; schema contracts/agent.v1alpha1.schema.json; parses append a deprecation notice to session.warnings). A top-level apiVersion key selects the legacy parser; its absence selects flat. Untrusted input: every value is a request that is validated and clamped server-side. Decoding is strict in both formats: unknown or misspelled fields are rejected with HTTP 400 (with did-you-mean and legacy-spelling hints on the flat path).

apiVersion.description: Legacy envelope only - must be "agents.digitalocean.com/v1alpha1", and its presence is what routes the document to the deprecated legacy parser. Flat-format manifests carry no version key (the endpoint owns the contract); required, with kind and spec, when authoring the legacy format.

description.description: Free-form description (max 1024 chars), stored and echoed back for Console / catalog surfaces.

name.description: Optional team-unique session name: 1-64 chars of letters, digits, '-', '.', '_', starting and ending alphanumeric; case-insensitive; must not be UUID-shaped. Omit to have the control plane generate one ("session-<agent-type>-<date-time>"). Unique among the team's ACTIVE (non-terminal) sessions; destroying a session frees its name for reuse.

budget.description: Accepted, not yet enforced (returns a warning). Advisory per-run ceilings, clamped server-side to tenant policy.

env.description: Non-secret guest env (debug-readable - never put secrets here; use spec.secrets). Reserved platform keys (TEAM_ID, SESSION_ID, SANDBOX_ID, CONTROL_PLANE_CALLBACK_URL, SANDBOX_TEMPLATE, SANDBOX_AGENT_WORKDIR, SIZE_SLUG, SANDBOX_IMAGE_ID, SANDBOX_OCI_REF, PLANO_PERMISSION_*) are rejected. Credential-looking values (dop_v1_..., sk-..., ghp_...) trigger a create-time warning.

memory.description: Accepted, not yet enforced (returns a warning).

mode.description: Explicit lifecycle discriminator. Defaults to "interactive" (spec.serving forbidden); "served" requires spec.serving.

model.description: Accepted, not yet enforced (returns a warning). Model routing (Plano); catalog-validated when enforcement lands.

runtime.description: Canonical adapter ids: claude-code | opencode | codex | cursor | hermes | codex-agentapi | custom. codex-agentapi is the OpenAI sandbox-provider runtime (DO runs codex exec-server; the agent loop lives at OpenAI) and pairs with the opaque spec.runtime.config block. codex-cli and cursor-cli are deprecated aliases (accepted with a create-time warning). The framework adapters (openai-agents, claude-agent-sdk, crewai, langgraph) are declared but not yet supported; CreateSession rejects them. adapter: custom requires the custom block.

config.description: OPAQUE, provider-specific runtime config. Only for adapter: codex-agentapi today, where it is the OpenAI Agents API create-session body (agent/environment/input) that doctl forwards verbatim to OpenAI's POST /v1/agents/sessions; harness-api stores and echoes it but never parses or validates its contents (so DO stays forward-compatible as OpenAI's schema evolves). The OpenAI session_id is passed on the create call (the openai_session_id query parameter), not in this block.

custom.description: BYO container; requires adapter: custom. image is required and should be digest-pinned.

egress.description: Requested egress policy (legacy envelope). unrestricted opts out of platform-default host allowlists and cannot combine with allow / allowIps / vpcUuid / subnetUuid. Absent or empty means no destination ACL (same as unrestricted). Flat authors prefer egress: unrestricted (scalar), a bare host list, or an object with allow_hosts / allow_ips / vpc_uuid / subnet_uuid. Platform host defaults are unioned only when allow names something; allowIps does not trigger that union (IP-only turns the destination ACL on without domain rules). VPC attachment is create-time immutable; ownership is verified at session create. Allowlists are a request only: the server intersects them with tenant + platform policy and can only narrow them.

unrestricted.description: When true, opts out of the platform-default host allowlist union. Mutually exclusive with allow / allowIps / vpcUuid / subnetUuid.

idleTimeoutSeconds.description: Inactivity suspend timeout. 0 means tenant policy default.

maxLifetimeSeconds.description: Hard wall-clock ceiling for the whole session, independent of activity. Accepted, not yet enforced (returns a warning).

mounts.description: Requested data mounts. Accepted, not yet enforced (returns a warning). accessKeyRef/secretKeyRef name declared tenantSecret slots in spec.secrets, validated at create; declare those slots with env: false so the keys stay mount-scoped and out of the guest env.

accessKeyRef.description: Names a declared tenantSecret slot in spec.secrets.

endpoint.description: Optional storage endpoint override; https:// only.

path.description: Absolute guest path the mount appears at.

secretKeyRef.description: Names a declared tenantSecret slot in spec.secrets.

sizeSlug.description: Requested sandbox size (catalog: GET /v2/agents/sessions/sandbox/sizes). Empty means the service default.

template.description: Optional sandbox template. Empty (or the legacy placeholder "coding") means "no preference": the template derives from the adapter.

secrets.description: Declared credential requirements. source tenantSecret is enforced today: value is write-only plaintext, extracted into Secrets Manager at create and never persisted or returned. source oauth requires provider, carries no value, and is accepted but not yet enforced. ref is legacy and ignored. env false keeps the resolved value out of the guest environment (mount-only slots).

env.description: Whether the resolved credential is injected into the guest env. Omitted means true; false is for mount-only slots (tenantSecret only).

value.description: Write-only tenantSecret plaintext; never persisted or returned.

serving.description: Present only when spec.mode is "served" (autoscaled fleet).

skills.description: Inline agent skills (SKILL.md shape): reusable markdown instructions the agent loads on demand, selected by description. Accepted, not yet enforced (returns a warning). Max 32 entries; instructions additionally capped at 256 KiB summed across the list so a valid manifest always fits the request-body limits. v0 is inline-only - remote skill sources come later as an additive field.

allowedTools.description: Advisory scoping of which tools the skill expects to use (experimental in the skills standard). NOT a security boundary - spec.permissions remains the only enforcement surface.

description.description: Load-bearing: the agent reads it to decide WHEN to load the skill (progressive disclosure); write it as "Use when ...". Max 1024 chars.

instructions.description: The markdown body (the content below the SKILL.md frontmatter). Max 32 KiB.

metadata.description: Optional string-map passthrough (e.g. author), rendered into the frontmatter verbatim.

name.description: Unique across the list; 1-64 chars of lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphen separators - no consecutive hyphens, per the Agent Skills spec (safe as a directory name at materialization).

tools.description: Accepted, not yet enforced (returns a warning). Exactly one of mcpServers or bundle.

items.description: Exactly one form per entry: CATALOG (ref - do.* only, the reserved DO-owned namespace, e.g. do.actions; there is no tenant-registered catalog) or INLINE (name + https url, optional brokered auth - the path for any non-DO server). Mixing forms is a 400. tools entries are individual tool names or toolbelt:<name>[@<int>] group references (catalog refs only) - selection only, disposition stays in spec.permissions. Inline hosts are not auto-allowed for egress - list them under spec.sandbox.egress.allow.

auth.description: Brokered credential for an INLINE server (invalid on the catalog form). secretRef names a declared tenantSecret slot in spec.secrets, validated at create; the slot is resolved server-side and sent as an HTTP header. Plaintext credentials are never accepted.

header.description: HTTP header the credential is sent in. Defaults to Authorization.

name.description: Inline server name (required with url): 1-64 chars of lowercase letters, digits, '-', '.', '_', starting/ending alphanumeric. Unique across the list. Must not start with do. (reserved for catalog refs).

preloadTools.description: Catalog form only. Individual tools (optional integer pin) advertised directly in the session MCP tools/list next to the action_search/action_invoke/action_code meta tools. Each entry must appear in tools when tools is set; toolbelt references are rejected. Every preloaded schema is in the model's context on every turn, so keep this to a handful of tools. Omitted means nothing is preloaded.

ref.description: DO-owned catalog reference (catalog form); do.* only, e.g. do.actions. Mutually exclusive with name/url/auth.

tools.description: Optional selection allowlist; omitted means all tools the server advertises. Each entry is an individual tool name with an optional integer version pin (e.g. web_search, execute_code@3) or a toolbelt reference - a server-defined named tool group written toolbelt:<name>[@<int>] (e.g. toolbelt:read-only@1; catalog refs only). Versions are integer pins (no semver). The server owns belt expansion; a pinned tool or belt attaches exactly that version, an unpinned one resolves at session create and is frozen for the session (no floating latest). Entries non-empty, unique per server. The selection bounds the session and is never preloaded into the session MCP tools/list; see preloadTools.

repos.description: GitHub OWNER/REPO entries, unique. The first entry becomes the session's repo_hint; the full list is the forward shape for multi-repo sessions.

id.description: A unique ID that can be used to identify and reference the alert.

alert_condition.description: Evaluation condition for the alert rule.

window.description:
Time window over which the metric is evaluated. Allowed values:

- `EVALUATION_WINDOW_1M` = `1m`
- `EVALUATION_WINDOW_5M` = `5m`
- `EVALUATION_WINDOW_10M` = `10m`
- `EVALUATION_WINDOW_15M` = `15m`
- `EVALUATION_WINDOW_30M` = `30m`
- `EVALUATION_WINDOW_1H` = `1h`

alert_instance.description: A read-only record of an alert rule firing against a resource.

id.description: A unique identifier for the alert instance.

last_notified_at.description: Time a notification was last sent for this alert instance.

last_triggered_at.description: Time the alert instance most recently fired.

resolved_at.description:
Time the alert instance resolved. Only present when `status` is
`resolved`.

resource_urn.description:
URN of the DigitalOcean resource the alert fired for. May be an empty
string for alerts fired on non-resource-bound signals (for example,
cluster/pod/namespace-scoped Kubernetes alerts).

rule_id.description: ID of the alert rule that fired this alert instance.

status.description: Current status of the alert instance.

triggered_at.description: Time the alert instance first fired.

value.description: The observed metric value that breached the threshold.

created_at.description: Time the alert rule was created.

id.description: A unique identifier for the alert rule.

status.description:
Current alert rule status. Allowed values:

- `ALERT_RULE_STATUS_ACTIVE` = active
- `ALERT_RULE_STATUS_PAUSED` = paused

updated_at.description: Time the alert rule was last updated.

alert_rule_request.description:
Create or update body for an alert rule. `spec` is required. `status` is
optional; create defaults to `ALERT_RULE_STATUS_ACTIVE`, and update keeps the
existing status when omitted.

status.description:
Desired alert rule status. Allowed values:

- `ALERT_RULE_STATUS_ACTIVE` = active
- `ALERT_RULE_STATUS_PAUSED` = paused

alert_rule_spec.description:
Spec for an Insights alert rule. On create, `name`, `query`, `thresholds`,
and at least one `notification_channels` binding are required. On update,
omit `notification_channels` to keep existing bindings; an explicit empty
list is rejected.

name.description: A human-readable name for the alert rule.

notification_channels.description: Notification channels to notify when the rule fires.

re_alert_duration.description:
Minimum wait before re-notifying a still-firing alert. Defaults to
`RE_ALERT_DURATION_4H` on create when omitted. Allowed values:

- `RE_ALERT_DURATION_30M` = `30m`
- `RE_ALERT_DURATION_1H` = `1h`
- `RE_ALERT_DURATION_4H` = `4h`

apiEpochResultSummary.description:
Aggregation across epochs when a run repeats each dataset row k times.
Only populated when epochs > 1; at epochs == 1 every number here would
equal overall_score_percent, so it is omitted rather than duplicated.

avg_at_k_percent.description:
Mean over rows of (passing epochs / scored epochs) for the star metric.
Equals overall_score_percent; this is the primary result for a
multi-epoch run ("how often does it work").

cons_at_k_percent.description:
Fraction of rows where a strict majority of scored epochs passed
("what does the model typically answer"). An even-k tie counts as fail.

epochs.description: Number of passes per dataset row (k).

pass_at_k_percent.description:
Unbiased estimate of the probability that at least one of k epochs
passes ("can it work at all, given retries"). Always the most generous
of the three.

per_epoch.description: Each epoch's own standalone score, persisted next to the aggregate.

rows_excluded.description:
Rows where every epoch failed or was skipped, so the row contributes to
no score. Not a random sample of difficulty — surface this explicitly.

rows_scored.description:
Rows with at least one scored epoch. The effective N behind every
percentage above; always display alongside them.

score_stddev_percent.description:
Population standard deviation of the k per-epoch scores below — the
signal for whether a difference between runs is real or noise.

apiModelEvaluationEpochAttempt.description:
ModelEvaluationEpochAttempt is one epoch's attempt at a dataset row,
nested under ModelEvaluationResult.epoch_results for multi-epoch runs.
Carries only the fields that vary per pass — row-identifying fields
(input/ground_truth/row_number) and candidate_model_name/uuid live once
on the parent ModelEvaluationResult and aren't repeated here.

metric_results.description: Per-metric scores and judge reasoning for this specific pass.

output.description: The response from the candidate model for this specific pass.

apiModelEvaluationPreset.description:
Model Evaluation Preset - a saved, reusable configuration for model
evaluation runs. Each section (dataset, judge, metrics, candidate, system
prompt) is independent and may be empty; sections the preset omits must be
supplied inline on the run that references it. Use `saved_sections` to tell
"section saved with empty value" apart from "section not saved at all" —
each section's scalar fields are left empty when the section was not saved.

candidate_model_name.description:
Model slug used to call the candidate model API. Empty when the CANDIDATE
section was not saved.

candidate_model_uuid.description:
UUID of the candidate model stored on this preset. Empty when the
CANDIDATE section was not saved. For DEDICATED candidates this is the
dedicated inference deployment UUID.

candidate_system_prompt.description:
System prompt / instructions to send to the candidate model. Empty when
the SYSTEM_PROMPT section was not saved (check `saved_sections`).

created_at.description: Timestamp when the preset was created.

dataset_name.description:
Display name of the dataset stored on this preset. Empty when the DATASET
section was not saved or the dataset no longer exists.

dataset_uuid.description:
UUID of the dataset stored on this preset. Empty when the DATASET section
was not saved (check `saved_sections`).

judge_model_name.description:
Display name of the judge model stored on this preset. Empty when the
JUDGE section was not saved or the model no longer exists.

judge_model_uuid.description:
UUID of the judge model stored on this preset. Empty when the JUDGE
section was not saved (check `saved_sections`).

metrics.description:
Metrics selected for this preset. Empty when the METRICS section was not
saved.

name.description: Name of the evaluation preset.

saved_sections.description:
Sections of the inline evaluation config that were persisted when this
preset was created. Use this to tell "section was saved with an empty
value" apart from "section was not saved" — scalar fields like
`dataset_uuid` or `candidate_system_prompt` are always emitted as the
empty string when the section was not saved.

apiModelEvaluationResult.description: Result for a single prompt in a model evaluation run.

epoch.description:
Which pass over this dataset row produced this result, 1-indexed (1 =
first pass). Always 0 (and omitted from JSON) when the run's epochs is 1
(the default) — per-attempt epoch numbering doesn't apply to
single-pass runs. When epochs > 1, this always reflects epoch 1 (see
epoch_results below).

epoch_results.description:
Present only when the run's epochs > 1: every pass over this row —
including epoch 1, duplicated here for convenience — keyed by
1-indexed "epoch1"/"epoch2"/"epoch3" labels. Mirrors the shape of the
downloadable results file's epochResults object. The top-level fields
above (output, metric_results, candidate_routed_task) always reflect
epoch 1, so single-epoch clients reading only those fields see no
difference when epochs > 1.

input.description: The input query sent to the candidate model.

metric_results.description: Per-metric scores and judge reasoning for this prompt.

output.description: The response from the candidate model.

row_number.description:
Which dataset row this result came from. Multiple results share a
row_number when epochs > 1: one per pass over that row.

apiModelEvaluationRunProgress.description:
Per-phase progress for a model evaluation run. The candidate phase invokes the
candidate model once per dataset row; the judge phase scores each
candidate-success row with the configured metrics. Counts grow as the run
advances; compare against total_rows to render a progress bar.

candidate_rows_evaluated.description: Dataset rows whose candidate model call has completed (success or failure).

judge_rows_evaluated.description:
Candidate-success rows the judge has finished (scored or skipped). Caps at
the number of candidate successes, which may be below total_rows.

total_rows.description: Total dataset rows for the run, sourced from the evaluation dataset.

apiModelPricing.description: Pricing per million tokens (aligns with existing ModelPrice pattern)

cache_read_input_price_per_million.description:
Per-million cache read rate for standard chat models (token_type "cache read input").
Multimodal models use text_cache_read_input_price_per_million / image_cache_read_input_price_per_million instead.

cache_write_1h_input_price_per_million.description: Price per million tokens written to the prompt cache with a 1-hour lifetime.

cache_write_5m_input_price_per_million.description: Price per million tokens written to the prompt cache with a 5-minute lifetime.

input_cache_read.description:
Cache read input price per single token. Equivalent to
cache_read_input_price_per_million.

price_per_image.description:
Unit-based pricing for non-token models (e.g., Fal AI image/video/audio
generation, speech models). At most one of these is typically populated
per model. Token-based models (chat, embeddings) leave all of these at 0
and populate input_price_per_million / output_price_per_million instead.

reasoning_price_per_million.description:
Price per million reasoning tokens. 0 if the model does not charge
separately for reasoning tokens.

text_input_price_per_million.description:
Per-million token rates for models that bill text vs image tokens separately
(e.g. OpenAI gpt-image-2). Standard chat models leave these at 0 and use
input_price_per_million / output_price_per_million instead. Values align
with usage token_type / internal/usage.Type string values for each meter.

 - MODEL_PRICING_TIER_BYOK: Pricing when using your own model API key.

apiPresetSaveSection.description:
Sections of an inline evaluation config that can be persisted as a reusable
preset. Each value names a self-contained group of fields; selecting a
section saves exactly the fields it owns and leaves the rest of the preset
empty so it can be merged with inline values on a future run.

 - PRESET_SAVE_SECTION_CANDIDATE: Candidate model identity (`candidate_model_uuid`, `candidate_model_source`,
`candidate_model_name`) and the non-prompt inference params
(`temperature`, `stop_token`, `reasoning_effort`).
 - PRESET_SAVE_SECTION_METRICS: The selected `metric_uuids` and the optional `star_metric`.
 - PRESET_SAVE_SECTION_JUDGE: The `judge_model_uuid`.
 - PRESET_SAVE_SECTION_DATASET: The `dataset_uuid`.
 - PRESET_SAVE_SECTION_SYSTEM_PROMPT: The candidate's `system_prompt` only. Independent of CANDIDATE so the
model + params and the prompt can be saved/replayed separately.

scenario sets (`source_kind=SCENARIO_SET_SOURCE_KIND_SIGNAL_GENERATED`).

apiScenarioSetSortField.description:
Sortable fields for listing scenario sets.

 - SCENARIO_SET_SORT_FIELD_CREATED_AT: Sort by creation date. Default.
 - SCENARIO_SET_SORT_FIELD_NAME: Sort by customer-supplied name (case-insensitive).
 - SCENARIO_SET_SORT_FIELD_STATUS: Sort by status using lifecycle order (generating → ready → terminal).
 - SCENARIO_SET_SORT_FIELD_SCENARIO_COUNT: Sort by scenario_count.
 - SCENARIO_SET_SORT_FIELD_UPDATED_AT: Sort by last update date.

apiScenarioSetSourceKind.description:
How a scenario set was created.

 - SCENARIO_SET_SOURCE_KIND_USER_UPLOAD: Created from uploaded or inline scenarios.
 - SCENARIO_SET_SOURCE_KIND_GOAL_GENERATED: Produced by goal-driven generation.
 - SCENARIO_SET_SOURCE_KIND_LIBRARY: Copied from a platform-curated library entry.
 - SCENARIO_SET_SOURCE_KIND_SIGNAL_GENERATED: Produced from a completed Signals export.

apiScenarioSetStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a scenario set. Uploaded sets are created as ready.
Generated sets start as generating and then become ready, failed, or
cancelled.

 - SCENARIO_SET_STATUS_GENERATING: Generation is in progress. The scenarios are not ready yet.
 - SCENARIO_SET_STATUS_READY: The scenario set is ready to use.
 - SCENARIO_SET_STATUS_FAILED: Generation failed. The scenario set has no readable scenarios.
 - SCENARIO_SET_STATUS_CANCELLED: Generation was cancelled before completion.

apiScenarioSortField.description:
Sortable fields for listing scenarios.

 - SCENARIO_SORT_FIELD_FILE_ORDER: Preserve original file order. Default.
 - SCENARIO_SORT_FIELD_NAME: Sort by scenario name (case-insensitive). Empty names sort last.
 - SCENARIO_SORT_FIELD_DESCRIPTION: Sort by scenario description (case-insensitive).

apiSimulationEpisodeSortField.description:
Sortable fields for listing simulation episodes.

 - SIMULATION_EPISODE_SORT_FIELD_CREATED_AT: Sort by creation date.
 - SIMULATION_EPISODE_SORT_FIELD_STATUS: Sort by episode status using lifecycle order.
 - SIMULATION_EPISODE_SORT_FIELD_VERDICT: Sort by verdict (nulls last).

apiSimulationEpisodeStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a single episode.

 - SIMULATION_EPISODE_STATUS_RUNNING: The episode is executing and a trajectory is available to retrieve.
 - SIMULATION_EPISODE_STATUS_FINISHED: The episode reached a stop condition and produced a verdict.
 - SIMULATION_EPISODE_STATUS_FAILED: The episode failed because of a cancel, timeout, or error.
 - SIMULATION_EPISODE_STATUS_PREPARING: The episode is allocated but its trajectory is not available yet.

apiSimulationEpisodeVerdict.description:
The judge's verdict for an episode.

 - SIMULATION_EPISODE_VERDICT_SUCCESS: The candidate agent satisfied the scenario's stopping criteria.
 - SIMULATION_EPISODE_VERDICT_FAILURE: The candidate agent did not satisfy the stopping criteria.
 - SIMULATION_EPISODE_VERDICT_INCONCLUSIVE: No conclusive verdict (e.g. max_turns reached without the judge finishing).

model_evaluation_run linked to this simulation run and dispatches the

reuses the simulation run's judge_model_uuid.

apiSimulationRunStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a simulation run.

 - SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_PENDING: Accepted and queued, not yet executing.
 - SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_RUNNING: Episodes are executing.
 - SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_SUCCEEDED: All episodes finished successfully.
 - SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_FAILED: The run failed, for example because of a timeout or workflow error.
 - SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_CANCELLED: The run was cancelled.
 - SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_EVALUATING: Episodes finished and an attached evaluation is running. Only reachable
when the create request included evaluation_config. When the evaluation
reaches a terminal status, its outcome is reflected in the simulation run
status.
 - SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_PARTIALLY_SUCCESSFUL: The simulation or its attached evaluation completed with a mixture of
successful and failed results.

apiSimulationTrajectoryStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of the trajectory. Distinct from episode status: the
trajectory is updated on every turn while the episode is executing.

 - SIMULATION_TRAJECTORY_STATUS_RUNNING: The episode loop is in progress; messages may grow on each poll.
 - SIMULATION_TRAJECTORY_STATUS_COMPLETED: The episode reached a stop condition and the trajectory is complete.
 - SIMULATION_TRAJECTORY_STATUS_FAILED: The episode failed before or during execution.
 - SIMULATION_TRAJECTORY_STATUS_CANCELLED: The episode was cancelled.

code.description:
A code identifier that represents the failing condition.

Failing conditions:
  - `incompatible_phase` - indicates that the deployment's phase is not suitable for rollback.
  - `incompatible_result` - indicates that the deployment's result is not suitable for rollback.
  - `exceeded_revision_limit` - indicates that the app has exceeded the rollback revision limits for its tier.
  - `app_pinned` - indicates that there is already a rollback in progress and the app is pinned.
  - `database_config_conflict` - indicates that the deployment's database config is different than the current config.
  - `region_conflict` - indicates that the deployment's region differs from the current app region.
  
Warning conditions:
  - `static_site_requires_rebuild` - indicates that the deployment contains at least one static site that will require a rebuild.
  - `image_source_missing_digest` - indicates that the deployment contains at least one component with an image source that is missing a digest.

If set to `true`, the app will **not** be cached at the edge (CDN). Enable this option if you want to manage CDN configuration yourself—whether by using an external CDN provider or by handling static content and caching within your app. This setting is also recommended for apps that require real-time data or serve dynamic content, such as those using Server-Sent Events (SSE) over GET, or hosting an MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server that utilizes SSE.

input.description:

leaf_certificate.description: The contents of a PEM-formatted public SSL certificate.

private_key.description: The contents of a PEM-formatted private-key corresponding to the SSL certificate.

dns_names.description: An array of fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) for which the certificate was issued. A certificate covering all subdomains can be issued using a wildcard (e.g. `*.example.com`).

chat_completion_chunk.description: Represents a streamed chunk of a chat completion response returned by the model, based on the provided input.

choices.description: A list of chat completion choices. Can contain more than one element if n is greater than 1. Can also be empty for the last chunk if you set stream_options include_usage to true.

finish_reason.description: The reason the model stopped generating tokens. stop if the model hit a natural stop point or a provided stop sequence, length if the maximum number of tokens specified in the request was reached, tool_calls if the model called a tool.

index.description: The index of the choice in the list of choices.

logprobs.description: Log probability information for the choice.

content.description: A list of message content tokens with log probability information.

refusal.description: A list of message refusal tokens with log probability information.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when the chat completion was created. Each chunk has the same timestamp.

id.description: A unique identifier for the chat completion. Each chunk has the same ID.

model.description: The model to generate the completion.

object.description: The object type, which is always chat.completion.chunk.

usage.description: An optional field that will only be present when you set stream_options include_usage to true in your request. When present, it contains a null value except for the last chunk which contains the token usage statistics for the entire request.

frequency_penalty.description: Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on their existing frequency in the text so far, decreasing the model's likelihood to repeat the same line verbatim.

logit_bias.description: Modify the likelihood of specified tokens appearing in the completion. Accepts a JSON object that maps tokens (specified by their token ID in the tokenizer) to an associated bias value from -100 to 100. Mathematically, the bias is added to the logits generated by the model prior to sampling. The exact effect will vary per model, but values between -1 and 1 should decrease or increase likelihood of selection; values like -100 or 100 should result in a ban or exclusive selection of the relevant token.

logprobs.description: Whether to return log probabilities of the output tokens or not. If true, returns the log probabilities of each output token returned in the content of message.

max_completion_tokens.description: The maximum number of completion tokens that may be used over the course of the run. The run will make a best effort to use only the number of completion tokens specified, across multiple turns of the run.

max_tokens.description: The maximum number of tokens that can be generated in the completion. The token count of your prompt plus max_tokens cannot exceed the model's context length.

messages.description: A list of messages comprising the conversation so far.

metadata.description: Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Keys are strings with a maximum length of 64 characters. Values are strings with a maximum length of 512 characters.

model.description: Model ID used to generate the response.

n.description: How many chat completion choices to generate for each input message. Note that you will be charged based on the number of generated tokens across all of the choices. Keep n as 1 to minimize costs.

presence_penalty.description: Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on whether they appear in the text so far, increasing the model's likelihood to talk about new topics.

reasoning_effort.description: Constrains effort on reasoning for reasoning models. Reducing reasoning effort can result in faster responses and fewer tokens used on reasoning in a response.

seed.description: If specified, the system will make a best effort to sample deterministically, such that repeated requests with the same seed and parameters should return the same result. Determinism is not guaranteed.

stop.description: Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating further tokens. The returned text will not contain the stop sequence.

stream.description: If set to true, the model response data will be streamed to the client as it is generated using server-sent events.

stream_options.description: Options for streaming response. Only set this when you set stream to true.

include_usage.description: If set, an additional chunk will be streamed before the data [DONE] message. The usage field on this chunk shows the token usage statistics for the entire request, and the choices field will always be an empty array.

temperature.description: What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. We generally recommend altering this or top_p but not both.

tool_choice.description: Controls which (if any) tool is called by the model. none means the model will not call any tool and instead generates a message. auto means the model can pick between generating a message or calling one or more tools. required means the model must call one or more tools. Specifying a particular tool via {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "my_function"}} forces the model to call that tool. none is the default when no tools are present. auto is the default if tools are present.

oneOf.description: Force a specific tool to be called.

name.description: The name of the function to call.

tools.description: A list of tools the model may call. Currently, only functions are supported as a tool.

top_logprobs.description: An integer between 0 and 20 specifying the number of most likely tokens to return at each token position, each with an associated log probability. logprobs must be set to true if this parameter is used.

top_p.description: An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered. We generally recommend altering this or temperature but not both.

user.description: A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help DigitalOcean to monitor and detect abuse.

chat_completion_response.description: Represents a chat completion response returned by model, based on the provided input.

choices.description: A list of chat completion choices. Can be more than one if n is greater than 1.

finish_reason.description: The reason the model stopped generating tokens. stop if the model hit a natural stop point or a provided stop sequence, length if the maximum number of tokens specified in the request was reached, tool_calls if the model called a tool.

index.description: The index of the choice in the list of choices.

logprobs.description: Log probability information for the choice.

content.description: A list of message content tokens with log probability information.

refusal.description: A list of message refusal tokens with log probability information.

enabled.description: A boolean value indicating whether the check is enabled/disabled.

checkpoint.description: Checkpoint is a durable capture of a session's live sandbox machine state bound to the event-log cursor at the cut. READY checkpoints seed forks (ForkSession) and rollback. Internal fields (team_id, the substrate checkpoint id, event_seq) are never serialized.

checkpoint_id.description: Public checkpoint id, stable for the checkpoint's lifetime (e.g. cp_9f2c1a4b).

error_message.description: Client-safe failure detail; set only when status is FAILED.

event_id.description: Event-log cursor (ULID) of the last event included in the cut; forks resume event replay from here.

label.description: Optional user-supplied label from CreateCheckpoint; empty when omitted.

size_bytes.description: Size of the captured machine state. 0 until the checkpoint reaches READY.

checkpoint-2.description: A checkpoint of a MicroVM's memory and disk. New MicroVMs created from a checkpoint start from that state.

created_at.description: When the checkpoint was created, in ISO 8601 format.

disk_bytes.description: The stored size of the checkpoint's disk, in bytes.

id.description: The unique ID of the checkpoint.

memory_bytes.description: The stored size of the checkpoint's memory, in bytes.

microvm_id.description: The ID of the MicroVM the checkpoint was taken from.

microvm_name.description: The name of the MicroVM the checkpoint was taken from.

name.description: The name of the checkpoint. If you do not set one, a name such as `checkpoint-20260929-143559` is generated.

region.description: The slug of the checkpoint's region.

status.description: The checkpoint's status. You can create MicroVMs from the checkpoint when it is `CHECKPOINT_AVAILABLE`.

checkpoint_kind.description: How the checkpoint came to exist: explicit - requested via CreateCheckpoint; implicit - minted automatically by the platform (on run completion, or when ForkSession is called without from_checkpoint_id).

checkpoint_status.description: Capture lifecycle: PENDING -> READY | FAILED. Only READY checkpoints are forkable/restorable. CreateCheckpoint blocks until terminal, so PENDING is only ever observable via list/get while a capture is in flight.

expanders.description:
Customizes expanders used by cluster-autoscaler.
The autoscaler will apply each expander from the provided list to narrow down the selection of node types created to scale up,
until either a single node type is left, or the list of expanders is exhausted.
If this flag is unset, autoscaler will use its default expander `random`.
Passing an empty list (_not_ `null`) will unset any previous expander customizations.

Available expanders:
- `random`: Randomly selects a node group to scale.
- `priority`: Selects the node group with the highest priority as per [user-provided configuration](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/kubernetes/how-to/autoscale/#configuring-priority-expander)
- `least_waste`: Selects the node group that will result in the least amount of idle resources.

scale_down_unneeded_time.description: Used to customize how long a node is unneeded before being scaled down.

scale_down_utilization_threshold.description: Used to customize when cluster autoscaler scales down non-empty nodes by setting the node utilization threshold.

definitions_session.description: Session is the user-facing record of a environment session + sandbox pair.

config_id.description: Durable Environment Config UUID the session was created from (inline manifests persist a config too, named after the session). Persisted and returned on create/get/list; absent only for sessions created before config references were stored.

fork_from_checkpoint_id.description: Lineage: harness-api checkpoint id (cp_<hex>) the child booted from at fork time. Drives OHP inherited-history replay on attach. Omitted/empty for root sessions and legacy forks created before this field was persisted.

fork_id.description: Lineage: branch label assigned when this session was created by ForkSession (or rollback's internal fork). Omitted/empty for root sessions.

idle_timeout_seconds.description: This session's own idle-pause timeout (manifest idle_timeout). Omitted when the session uses the deployment-wide default.

keep_warm.description: Session is exempt from idle auto-pause (manifest keep_warm, or the agent-kind default: hermes sessions keep warm). Pause requests against such a session are rejected with 409. Omitted when false.

last_event_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent event in this session's canonical stream. Drives the inactivity policy that destroys idle sessions.

name.description: User-assignable display name, unique per team among non-terminal sessions. Usable in place of session_id by clients (doctl / Console resolve it to the id via the ListSessions ?name= filter; the {session_id} path stays UUID-only). Supplied via the environment-spec metadata.name, or auto-generated ("session-<agent-type>-<date-time>") when omitted.

openai_environment_id.description: OpenAI Agents API environment id (env_…), captured from the resolved CODEX_ENVIRONMENT_ID guest env value. Populated only for AGENT_KIND_OPENAI_CODEX sessions. Non-secret correlation metadata.

openai_session_id.description: OpenAI Agents API session id (sess_…) this DO sandbox hosts. Populated only for AGENT_KIND_OPENAI_CODEX sessions (empty otherwise). Non-secret correlation metadata; a client (doctl agents attach) reads it to bridge to the OpenAI session. See docs/design/openai-sandbox-provider.md.

parent_session_id.description: Lineage: id of the session this one was forked from. Omitted/empty for root (non-fork) sessions.

pause_reason.description: Why this session is paused. Present only when status is SESSION_STATUS_PAUSED; omitted otherwise. Known values: manual (PauseSession RPC), idle (inactivity auto-pause), low_balance (prepay gate). Clients should treat an unrecognized value as an opaque reason string.

repo_hint.description: Optional repository hint supplied at session creation (first spec.workspace.repos entry of the manifest). Not authoritative; the agent may change repos in-session.

resume_on_topoff.description: Session consents to being resumed automatically when the team's prepayment balance is restored after a low-balance pause. Defaults to false at create time; may be toggled later via PATCH /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id} (resume_on_topoff only). Only a session paused with reason low_balance whose latest run did not complete is ever resumed automatically - a session the customer paused themselves, or one that idled out, stays paused regardless. Not an environment-spec field, and forks do not inherit it. Omitted when false.

sandbox_id.description: Sandbox identity for support / debugging. Informational; omitted until a sandbox is allocated.

warnings.description: Non-fatal advisories computed from the manifest at create time: one entry per populated accepted-but-not-yet-enforced section (flat names: secrets, model, tools, memory, budget, max_lifetime, mounts; legacy manifests get the corresponding spec.* paths), a deprecation entry when a legacy-envelope manifest or an adapter alias (codex-cli, cursor-cli) is used, and a heuristic entry per credential-looking spec.env value. Populated on the CreateSession response only.

eviction_policy_model.description:
A string specifying the desired eviction policy for a Caching or Valkey cluster.

- `noeviction`: Don't evict any data, returns error when memory limit is reached.
- `allkeys_lru:` Evict any key, least recently used (LRU) first.
- `allkeys_random`: Evict keys in a random order.
- `volatile_lru`: Evict keys with expiration only, least recently used (LRU) first.
- `volatile_random`: Evict keys with expiration only in a random order.
- `volatile_ttl`: Evict keys with expiration only, shortest time-to-live (TTL) first.

argv.description: Program and arguments. Required and non-empty; run directly, with no shell interpretation.

Records are fetched in batches, and if the first record batch in the first non-empty partition of the fetch is larger than this value, the record batch will still be returned to ensure that progress can be made. As such, this is not an absolute maximum.

schema_registry.description: Enable creation of schema registry for the Kafka cluster. Schema_registry only works with General Purpose - Dedicated CPU plans.

socket_request_max_bytes.description: The maximum number of bytes in a socket request (defaults to 104857600).

transaction_remove_expired_transaction_c.description: The interval at which to remove transactions that have expired due to transactional.id.expiration.ms passing (defaults to 3600000 (1 hour)).

transaction_state_log_segment_bytes.description: The transaction topic segment bytes should be kept relatively small in order to facilitate faster log compaction and cache loads (defaults to 104857600 (100 mebibytes)).

cleanup_policy.description: The cleanup_policy sets the retention policy to use on log segments. 'delete' will discard old segments when retention time/size limits are reached. 'compact' will enable log compaction, resulting in retention of the latest value for each key.

compression_type.description: The compression_type specifies the compression type of the topic.

delete_retention_ms.description: The delete_retention_ms specifies how long (in ms) to retain delete tombstone markers for topics.

file_delete_delay_ms.description: The file_delete_delay_ms specifies the time (in ms) to wait before deleting a file from the filesystem.

flush_messages.description: The flush_messages specifies the number of messages to accumulate on a log partition before messages are flushed to disk.

flush_ms.description: The flush_ms specifies the maximum time (in ms) that a message is kept in memory before being flushed to disk.

index_interval_bytes.description: The index_interval_bytes specifies the number of bytes between entries being added into te offset index.

max_compaction_lag_ms.description: The max_compaction_lag_ms specifies the maximum amount of time (in ms) that a message will remain uncompacted. This is only applicable if the logs are have compaction enabled.

max_message_bytes.description: The max_messages_bytes specifies the largest record batch size (in bytes) that can be sent to the server.  This is calculated after compression if compression is enabled.

message_down_conversion_enable.description: The message_down_conversion_enable specifies whether down-conversion of message formats is enabled to satisfy consumer requests. When 'false', the broker will not perform conversion for consumers expecting older message formats. The broker will respond with an `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION` error for consume requests from these older clients.

message_format_version.description: The message_format_version specifies the message format version used by the broker to append messages to the logs. The value of this setting is assumed to be 3.0-IV1 if the broker protocol version is 3.0 or higher. By setting a  particular message format version, all existing messages on disk must be smaller or equal to the specified version.

message_timestamp_type.description: The message_timestamp_type specifies whether to use the message create time or log append time as the timestamp on a message.

min_cleanable_dirty_ratio.description: The min_cleanable_dirty_ratio specifies the frequency of log compaction (if enabled) in relation to duplicates present in the logs. For example, at 0.5, at most 50% of the log could be duplicates before compaction would begin.

min_compaction_lag_ms.description: The min_compaction_lag_ms specifies the minimum time (in ms) that a message will remain uncompacted in the log. Only relevant if log compaction is enabled.

min_insync_replicas.description: The min_insync_replicas specifies the number of replicas that must ACK a write for the write to be considered successful.

preallocate.description: The preallocate specifies whether a file should be preallocated on disk when creating a new log segment.

retention_bytes.description: The retention_bytes specifies the maximum size of the log (in bytes) before deleting messages. -1 indicates that there is no limit.

retention_ms.description: The retention_ms specifies the maximum amount of time (in ms) to keep a message before deleting it.

segment_bytes.description: The segment_bytes specifies the maximum size of a single log file (in bytes).

segment_jitter_ms.description: The segment_jitter_ms specifies the maximum random jitter subtracted from the scheduled segment roll time to avoid thundering herds of segment rolling.

segment_ms.description: The segment_ms specifies the period of time after which the log will be forced to roll if the segment file isn't full. This ensures that retention can delete or compact old data.

offset.description: The current offset of the consumer group.

earliest_offset.description: The earliest consumer offset amongst consumer groups.

algorithm.description: This field has been deprecated. You can no longer specify an algorithm for load balancers.

created_at.description: A time value given in ISO8601 combined date and time format that represents when the load balancer was created.

disable_lets_encrypt_dns_records.description: A boolean value indicating whether to disable automatic DNS record creation for Let's Encrypt certificates that are added to the load balancer.

domains.description: An array of objects specifying the domain configurations for a Global load balancer.

enable_backend_keepalive.description: A boolean value indicating whether HTTP keepalive connections are maintained to target Droplets.

enable_proxy_protocol.description: A boolean value indicating whether PROXY Protocol is in use.

forwarding_rules.description: An array of objects specifying the forwarding rules for a load balancer.

http_idle_timeout_seconds.description: An integer value which configures the idle timeout for HTTP requests to the target droplets.

id.description: A unique ID that can be used to identify and reference a load balancer.

ipv6.description: An attribute containing the public-facing IPv6 address of the load balancer.

name.description: A human-readable name for a load balancer instance.

network.description: A string indicating whether the load balancer should be external or internal. Internal load balancers have no public IPs and are only accessible to resources on the same VPC network. This property cannot be updated after creating the load balancer.

network_stack.description: A string indicating whether the load balancer will support IPv4 or both IPv4 and IPv6 networking. This property cannot be updated after creating the load balancer.

project_id.description: The ID of the project that the load balancer is associated with. If no ID is provided at creation, the load balancer associates with the user's default project. If an invalid project ID is provided, the load balancer will not be created.

redirect_http_to_https.description: A boolean value indicating whether HTTP requests to the load balancer on port 80 will be redirected to HTTPS on port 443.

size.description:
This field has been replaced by the `size_unit` field for all regions except in AMS2, NYC2, and SFO1. Each available load balancer size now equates to the load balancer having a set number of nodes.
* `lb-small` = 1 node
* `lb-medium` = 3 nodes
* `lb-large` = 6 nodes

You can resize load balancers after creation up to once per hour. You cannot resize a load balancer within the first hour of its creation.

size_unit.description: How many nodes the load balancer contains. Each additional node increases the load balancer's ability to manage more connections. Load balancers can be scaled up or down, and you can change the number of nodes after creation up to once per hour. This field is currently not available in the AMS2, NYC2, or SFO1 regions. Use the `size` field to scale load balancers that reside in these regions.

status.description: A status string indicating the current state of the load balancer. This can be `new`, `active`, or `errored`.

subnet_uuid.description: A string specifying the UUID of the VPC subnet to which the load balancer is assigned.

target_load_balancer_ids.description: An array containing the UUIDs of the Regional load balancers to be used as target backends for a Global load balancer.

tls_cipher_policy.description: A string indicating the policy for the TLS cipher suites used by the load balancer. The possible values are `DEFAULT` or `STRONG`. The default value is `DEFAULT`.

type.description: A string indicating whether the load balancer should be a standard regional HTTP load balancer, a regional network load balancer that routes traffic at the TCP/UDP transport layer, or a global load balancer.

vpc_uuid.description: A string specifying the UUID of the VPC to which the load balancer is assigned.

load_balancer_create.description: The request schema for creating a load balancer. This is the same as the update schema with the addition of the create-only `ip` field, which assigns a Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) address to the load balancer.

droplet_ids.description: An array containing the IDs of the Droplets assigned to the load balancer.

tag.description: The name of a Droplet tag corresponding to Droplets assigned to the load balancer.

ip.description: An optional IP address to assign to the load balancer from one of your Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) prefixes. The address must be an unassigned BYOIP address on your account in the same region as the load balancer. If omitted, DigitalOcean assigns a public IP address automatically. This field is only applied when creating the load balancer, cannot be changed afterward, and is not supported for `GLOBAL` or `INTERNAL` load balancers.

logs_field_ref.description: A reference to a logical field for filters, ordering, grouping, or facets.

The dotted shorthands `service.name`, `resource.type`, and `resource.urn` are also supported. Arbitrary resource or log attributes can be accessed with `ResourceAttributes['key']` or `LogAttributes['key']`.

scope.description: The attribute scope to resolve the field against. Omit to let the server apply its default mapping for the field name.

logs_filter_condition.description: A single field comparison in a logs filter expression.

text_search.description: A substring search across the log body, service name, and resource URN.

logs_filter_value.description: A typed literal or list value for a filter condition. Exactly one kind is set per message.

logs_log_record.description: A single log record returned by a logs search.

body.description: The log message body. Omitted when empty.

resource.description: Resource attributes associated with the log.

service_name.description: The service name that emitted the log.

logs_order_by.description: A sort clause for logs search results.

direction.description: The sort direction. Omit to use the server default.

logs_pagination_request.description: Opaque keyset pagination request. Cursors are only valid when ordering by `timestamp` alone.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 100 and is clamped to 1000.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor to fetch the next page.

order_by.description: Sort clauses applied to the result set.

logs_search_response.description: Response body for a logs search.

data.description: Matching log records. Omitted when no records match.

logs_time_instant.description: A single point in time. Exactly one value form is set per message.

absolute.description: An absolute timestamp. Accepts RFC3339/RFC3339Nano strings or Unix seconds/nanoseconds as decimal strings.

relative.description: A relative time. Use `now` for the current time, a bare duration such as `1h` or `7d` to look back from now, or an offset such as `now-1h` or `now+30m`. Supported units are `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`, and `w`.

unix_nano.description: A Unix nanosecond timestamp, encoded as a string to preserve 64-bit precision.

sink_type.description:
Type of logsink integration.

- Use `datadog` for Datadog integration **only with MongoDB clusters**.
- For non-MongoDB clusters, use `rsyslog` for general syslog forwarding.
- Other supported types include `elasticsearch` and `opensearch`.

More details about the configuration can be found in the `config` property.

duration.description: The duration of the maintenance window policy in human-readable format.

start_time.description: The start time in UTC of the maintenance window policy in 24-hour clock format / HH:MM notation (e.g., `15:00`).

mcp_server.description: MCP server registered by your team. It never contains secret material.

createdAt.description: When the server was registered, in RFC 3339 format.

credentialRef.description: The secret reference supplied at registration when source=secret, or the team's OAuth credential ID when source=connection. Empty when the server was registered with an `api_key`, whose storage DigitalOcean manages.

credentialRefSource.description: How requests to the server authenticate: none, secret (a key or token sent in the Authorization header), or connection (each user's own OAuth authorization).

protocolVersion.description: MCP protocol revision negotiated with the server.

syncError.description: Why the latest discovery failed; empty after a successful one.

syncStatus.description: Outcome of the latest discovery: pending (no discovery has finished yet), ok, failed, or `unsupported_protocol`. It is not reset while a resync runs.

toolCount.description: Number of tools discovered on the server, whether enabled or not.

updatedAt.description: When the server was last modified, in RFC 3339 format.

mcp_server_create.description: Describes an MCP server to register.

api_key.description: For `credentialRefSource` secret: the key or token itself. DigitalOcean stores it; it is write-only and no response returns it. Set exactly one of `credentialRef` and `api_key`.

credentialRef.description: For `credentialRefSource` secret: a reference to a secret your team stores with DigitalOcean. Must match `^`[A-Za-z0-9]``[A-Za-z0-9:/_.-]`{0,254}$`. Set exactly one of `credentialRef` and `api_key`.

credentialRefSource.description: How requests to the server authenticate: none (the default), secret, or connection. With secret, the value from `credentialRef` or `api_key` is sent in the Authorization header, prefixed with "Bearer " unless it already contains a space.

description.description: Optional description shown on the server's catalog card. At most 1024 characters.

endpoint.description: HTTPS URL of the server's MCP endpoint. Its host must resolve only to public IP addresses. Required.

oauth_authorization_ttl_seconds.description:
How long, in seconds, a user's authorization may be reused before they must consent again. Optional;
0 means 30 days, and the maximum is 100 years.

Authorizations are not refreshed automatically, so this window, not the provider's token lifetime,
decides how often a user is sent back through consent. Set it no longer than the provider's own
token lifetime, so the prompt arrives before a tool call fails against an expired token.

oauth_authorize_url.description: Required for `credentialRefSource` connection: the OAuth authorization endpoint. It must use the endpoint's scheme and port, on the endpoint's host or another host under the same registrable domain.

oauth_client_id.description: Required for `credentialRefSource` connection: the client ID of your team's OAuth client for the server. Each user of the server then authorizes individually.

oauth_client_secret.description: Required for `credentialRefSource` connection. Write-only; no response returns it.

oauth_scopes.description: Required for `credentialRefSource` connection: the scopes to request from each user, 1 to 64 of them.

oauth_token_url.description: Required for `credentialRefSource` connection: the OAuth token endpoint, under the same rules as `oauth_authorize_url`.

serverRef.description: Identifier for the server, unique within your team. Must match `^`[a-z]``[a-z0-9-]`{0,63}$`.

transport.description: Optional. `streamable_http`, the default and only accepted value.

user_id.description: Required for a server registered with `credentialRefSource` connection: discovery reaches the server as this user, through their connection, because such a server has no team-wide credential. Ignored otherwise.

metrics_query.description:
Metrics query that the alert rule evaluates. `metric` must be a dotted
OpenTelemetry name (for example `do.droplets.cpu_utilization`). Underscored
Prometheus-style names are rejected. When `resource_urns` is omitted or empty,
the rule is not scoped to specific resources.

filters.description: Optional label filters applied to the metric series.
