Dotted OpenTelemetry metric name to evaluate
(for example `do.droplets.cpu_utilization`).

resource_urns.description:
Optional list of DigitalOcean resource URNs the rule applies to. Empty or
omitted means the rule is not scoped to specific resources.

tags.description: Optional resource tags used to select matching resources.

metric.description: An object containing the metric's labels. These labels are key/value pairs that vary depending on the metric being queried. For example, load balancer metrics contain a `lb_id` label, while Droplet metrics contain a `host_id` label, and App Platform metrics contain a `app_component` label.

values.description: An array of values for the metric.

microvm.description: A MicroVM. All fields are set at creation. There is no update endpoint.

auto_resume.description: Whether an HTTP request, command, or console session resumes the MicroVM when it is paused.

created_at.description: When the MicroVM was created, in ISO 8601 format.

failure_reason.description: Why the MicroVM failed. Present only when `state` is `failed`.
failure_reason.example: workload container exited (code 0): exited with code 0

http_protocol.description: The protocol the MicroVM's HTTP port serves. `null` if the protocol was not set when the MicroVM was created.

id.description: The unique ID of the MicroVM.

name.description: The name of the MicroVM. Must be unique in the region and contain 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.

networking.description: `public` sends outbound traffic through a shared NAT gateway. `vpc` places the MicroVM in the VPC network set by `vpc_uuid`.

ports.description: The guest ports declared on the MicroVM, including the HTTP port. During the public preview, only the HTTP port is reachable through the MicroVM's endpoint.

region.description: The slug of the region the MicroVM is in.

tags.description: The tags applied to the MicroVM.

urls.description: The MicroVM's HTTPS endpoints. The entry with `default` set to `true` is the endpoint for the HTTP port.

vpc_uuid.description: The ID of a VPC network in the same region that belongs to your team. Present only when `networking` is `vpc`.

microvm_auto_pause.description: Automatic pause settings. A MicroVM always pauses after it is idle for `idle_timeout`. Sending `enabled` set to `false` is rejected.

enabled.description: Whether auto-pause is on. Always `true`.

idle_timeout.description: How long the MicroVM is idle before it pauses, as a duration such as `30s`, `5m`, or `1h`. Defaults to `5m`. The maximum is `4h`. Responses show the duration in the form `5m0s`.

microvm_create.description: The request body for creating a MicroVM. With `source.oci_ref`, `region` and `size` are required. With `source.checkpoint_id`, the MicroVM inherits the checkpoint's region, size, container image, and environment variables, and a different `region` or `size`, or any `environment`, is rejected.

auto_resume.description: Whether an HTTP request, command, or console session resumes the MicroVM when it is paused. Set to `false` to require a manual resume.

environment.description: Environment variables passed into the MicroVM at boot, as key and value pairs. Not returned in responses.

http_port.description: The guest port the workload serves HTTP on. Defaults to `8080`. Not returned in responses. When creating from a checkpoint without `ports`, must be one of the checkpoint's ports.

http_protocol.description: The protocol the HTTP port serves.

name.description: The name of the MicroVM. Must be unique in the region and contain 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.

networking.description: `public` sends outbound traffic through a shared NAT gateway. `vpc` places the MicroVM in the VPC network set by `vpc_uuid`.

ports.description: The guest ports to declare, up to five. Must include `http_port`. Defaults to only the HTTP port. During the public preview, only the HTTP port is reachable through the MicroVM's endpoint.

region.description: The slug of the region to create the MicroVM in. Required with `source.oci_ref`.

tags.description: Tags to apply to the MicroVM.

vpc_uuid.description: The ID of a VPC network in the same region that belongs to your team. Required when `networking` is `vpc`.

message.description: A human-readable description of the error.

microvm_options.description: The default region, sizes, prices, account limits, and features available to your team.

max_disk_bytes.description: The maximum disk per MicroVM, in bytes.

max_idle_timeout_seconds.description: The maximum auto-pause idle timeout, in seconds.

max_memory_bytes.description: The maximum memory per MicroVM, in bytes.

max_total_count.description: The maximum number of MicroVMs, counting both running and paused MicroVMs.

default_region.description: The slug of the region MicroVMs are created in by default.

features.description: Features and whether they are enabled for your team.

enabled.description: Whether the feature is enabled.

name.description: The name of the feature.

price_per_gib_bandwidth.description: The price per GiB of outbound data transfer.

price_per_gib_memory_hour.description: The price per GiB of memory per hour of running time.

price_per_gib_storage_month.description: The price per GiB-month of disk and checkpoint storage.

price_per_vcpu_hour.description: The price per vCPU per hour of running time.

sizes.description: The sizes available to your team.

available.description: Whether the size is available on your team's plan.

disk.description: The size of the disk, in GB.

memory.description: The amount of memory, in MiB.

pricing.description: The compute price of the size.

price_per_hour.description: The price per hour of running time, in USD.

price_per_month.description: The price for running continuously for a month (730 hours), in USD.

regions.description: The slugs of the regions the size is available in.

microvm_size.description: The MicroVM's size. `cpu` and `memory` must be one of the pairs `1`/`2048`, `2`/`4096`, `8`/`16384`, or `16`/`32768`. The size sets the disk, which is returned in responses.

disk.description: The size of the disk, in GB. Set by the size.

memory.description: The amount of memory, in MiB.

microvm_source.description: What the MicroVM runs. Set exactly one of `oci_ref` or `checkpoint_id`.

checkpoint_id.description: The ID of a checkpoint to create the MicroVM from. The new MicroVM inherits the checkpoint's region, size, container image, and environment variables.

oci_ref.description: A reference to a `linux/amd64` container image in the form `registry/repository:tag`. The image can be public, such as an image on Docker Hub, or private in your team's DigitalOcean Container Registry.

microvm_url.description: An HTTPS endpoint for one of the MicroVM's ports.

default.description: Whether this is the endpoint for the MicroVM's HTTP port.

hostname.description: The endpoint's hostname. Empty until provisioning finishes. Requests to the endpoint must include a DigitalOcean API token with the `microvm:access` scope in the `Authorization` header.

port.description: The guest port the endpoint serves.

status.description: `PENDING` until provisioning finishes, then `ACTIVE`.

model.description: Describes a model offering that can be used with the API.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the model was created.

id.description: The model identifier, which can be referenced in the API endpoints.

object.description: The object type, which is always "model".

owned_by.description: The organization that owns the model.

model_deployment_spec.description: Configuration for a single model deployment.

model_id.description: Used to identify an existing deployment when updating; empty means create new.

default_read_concern.description: Specifies the default consistency behavior of reads from the database. Data that is returned from the query with may or may not have been acknowledged by all nodes in the replicaset depending on this value.  Learn more [here](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern/).

default_write_concern.description: Describes the level of acknowledgment requested from MongoDB for write operations clusters. This field can set to either `majority` or a number `0...n` which will describe the number of nodes that must acknowledge the write operation before it is fully accepted. Setting to `0` will request no acknowledgement of the write operation.  Learn more [here](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/write-concern/).

slow_op_threshold_ms.description: Operations that run for longer than this threshold are considered slow which are then recorded to the diagnostic logs.  Higher log levels (verbosity) will record all operations regardless of this threshold on the primary node.  *Changing this parameter will lead to a restart of the MongoDB service.* Learn more [here](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options/#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.slowOpThresholdMs).

transaction_lifetime_limit_seconds.description: Specifies the lifetime of multi-document transactions. Transactions that exceed this limit are considered expired and will be  aborted by a periodic cleanup process. The cleanup process runs every `transactionLifetimeLimitSeconds/2 seconds` or at least  once every 60 seconds. *Changing this parameter will lead to a restart of the MongoDB service.* Learn more [here](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters/#mongodb-parameter-param.transactionLifetimeLimitSeconds).

verbosity.description: The log message verbosity level. The verbosity level determines the amount of Informational and Debug messages MongoDB outputs. 0 includes informational messages while 1...5 increases the level to include debug messages. *Changing this parameter will lead to a restart of the MongoDB service.* Learn more [here](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options/#mongodb-setting-systemLog.verbosity).

name.description: A globally unique name for the container registry. Must be lowercase and be composed only of numbers, letters and `-`, up to a limit of 63 characters.

region.description: Slug of the region where registry data is stored. When not provided, a region will be selected.

subscription_tier_slug.description: The slug of the subscription tier to sign up for. Valid values can be retrieved using the options endpoint.

automatic_sp_privileges.description: When enabled, grants `EXECUTE` and `ALTER ROUTINE` privileges to the creator of a stored routine. When disabled, these privileges are not granted automatically.

backup_hour.description: The hour of day (in UTC) when backup for the service starts. New backup only starts if previous backup has already completed.

backup_minute.description: The minute of the backup hour when backup for the service starts. New backup  only starts if previous backup has already completed.

binlog_retention_period.description: The minimum amount of time, in seconds, to keep binlog entries before deletion.  This may be extended for services that require binlog entries for longer than the default, for example if using the MySQL Debezium Kafka connector.

connect_timeout.description: The number of seconds that the mysqld server waits for a connect packet before responding with bad handshake.

default_time_zone.description: Default server time zone, in the form of an offset from UTC (from -12:00 to +12:00), a time zone name (EST), or 'SYSTEM' to use the MySQL server default.

div_precision_increment.description: The number of digits by which to increase the scale of the result of division operations performed with the `/` operator.

end_markers_in_json.description: When enabled, the JSON output of `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON` includes end markers for nested structures.

eq_range_index_dive_limit.description: The number of equality ranges in an equality comparison condition when the optimizer should switch from using index dives to index statistics.

group_concat_max_len.description: The maximum permitted result length, in bytes, for the GROUP_CONCAT() function.

information_schema_stats_expiry.description: The time, in seconds, before cached statistics expire.

innodb_adaptive_hash_index.description: When enabled, InnoDB uses an adaptive hash index to speed up equality lookups. The optimal setting is workload-dependent: it can improve performance for some workloads, but under high concurrency the associated latch can become a contention point, in which case disabling it may improve throughput. Default is true.

innodb_change_buffer_max_size.description: Specifies the maximum size of the InnoDB change buffer as a percentage of the buffer pool.

innodb_flush_neighbors.description:
Specifies whether flushing a page from the InnoDB buffer pool also flushes other dirty pages in the same extent.
  - 0 — disables this functionality, dirty pages in the same extent are not flushed.
  - 1 — flushes contiguous dirty pages in the same extent.
  - 2 — flushes dirty pages in the same extent.

innodb_ft_enable_stopword.description: When enabled, the InnoDB FULLTEXT index stopword list is used. Disabled by default when a custom stopword table is configured.

innodb_ft_max_token_size.description: The maximum length of words that an InnoDB FULLTEXT index stores. Changing this parameter will lead to a restart of the MySQL service.

innodb_ft_min_token_size.description: The minimum length of words that an InnoDB FULLTEXT index stores.

innodb_ft_num_word_optimize.description: The number of words to process during each OPTIMIZE TABLE operation on an InnoDB FULLTEXT index.

innodb_ft_result_cache_limit.description: The InnoDB FULLTEXT index query result cache size limit, in bytes.

innodb_ft_server_stopword_table.description: The InnoDB FULLTEXT index stopword list for all InnoDB tables.

innodb_ft_user_stopword_table.description: The InnoDB FULLTEXT index stopword list for user-created FULLTEXT indexes. Must be in the form `db_name/table_name`. Set to `null` to clear a previously configured value.

innodb_lock_wait_timeout.description: The time, in seconds, that an InnoDB transaction waits for a row lock. before giving up.

innodb_log_buffer_size.description: The size of the buffer, in bytes, that InnoDB uses to write to the log files. on disk.

innodb_online_alter_log_max_size.description: The upper limit, in bytes, of the size of the temporary log files used during online DDL operations for InnoDB tables.

innodb_optimize_fulltext_only.description: When enabled, OPTIMIZE TABLE rebuilds only the InnoDB FULLTEXT index, not the table itself.

innodb_print_all_deadlocks.description: When enabled, records information about all deadlocks in InnoDB user transactions  in the error log. Disabled by default.

innodb_read_io_threads.description: The number of I/O threads for read operations in InnoDB. Changing this parameter will lead to a restart of the MySQL service.

innodb_rollback_on_timeout.description: When enabled, transaction timeouts cause InnoDB to abort and roll back the entire transaction.

innodb_thread_concurrency.description: Defines the maximum number of threads permitted inside of InnoDB. A value of 0 (the default) is interpreted as infinite concurrency (no limit). This variable is intended for performance  tuning on high concurrency systems.

innodb_write_io_threads.description: The number of I/O threads for write operations in InnoDB. Changing this parameter will lead to a restart of the MySQL service.

interactive_timeout.description: The time, in seconds, the server waits for activity on an interactive. connection before closing it.

internal_tmp_mem_storage_engine.description: The storage engine for in-memory internal temporary tables.

log_output.description: Defines the destination for logs. Can be `INSIGHTS`, `TABLE`, or both (`INSIGHTS,TABLE`), or `NONE` to disable logs. To specify both destinations, use `INSIGHTS,TABLE` (order matters). Default is NONE.

long_query_time.description: The time, in seconds, for a query to take to execute before  being captured by slow_query_logs. Default is 10 seconds.

max_allowed_packet.description: The size of the largest message, in bytes, that can be received by the server. Default is 67108864 (64M).

max_execution_time.description: The execution timeout for `SELECT` statements, in milliseconds. A value of `0` disables the timeout (no limit).

max_heap_table_size.description: The maximum size, in bytes, of internal in-memory tables. Also set tmp_table_size. Default is 16777216 (16M)

max_seeks_for_key.description: Limits the assumed maximum number of seeks when looking up rows based on a key. Lower values cause the query optimizer to prefer indexes over table scans for non-covering indexes.

net_buffer_length.description: Start sizes of connection buffer and result buffer, must be multiple of 1024. Changing this parameter will lead to a restart of the MySQL service.

net_read_timeout.description: The time, in seconds, to wait for more data from an existing connection. aborting the read.

net_write_timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for a block to be written to a connection before aborting the write.

optimizer_prune_level.description: Controls the heuristics applied during query optimization to prune less promising partial plans from the optimizer search space. `0` disables pruning and `1` enables it.

optimizer_search_depth.description: The maximum depth of search performed by the query optimizer. Smaller values can reduce compilation time for large joins; a value of `0` lets the server automatically pick a reasonable value.

optimizer_switch.description: Controls query optimizer behavior as a comma-separated list of `option=value` pairs, or `default` to restore server defaults. Each value must be `on`, `off`, or `default`.

slow_query_log.description: When enabled, captures slow queries. When disabled, also truncates the mysql.slow_log table. Default is false.

sort_buffer_size.description: The sort buffer size, in bytes, for ORDER BY optimization. Default is 262144. (256K).

sql_mode.description: Global SQL mode. If empty, uses MySQL server defaults. Must only include uppercase alphabetic characters, underscores, and commas.

sql_require_primary_key.description: Require primary key to be defined for new tables or old tables modified with ALTER TABLE and fail if missing. It is recommended to always have primary keys because various functionality may break if any large table is missing them.

tmp_table_size.description: The maximum size, in bytes, of internal in-memory tables. Also set max_heap_table_size. Default is 16777216 (16M).

wait_timeout.description: The number of seconds the server waits for activity on a noninteractive connection before closing it.

windowing_use_high_precision.description: When enabled, window functions use a higher precision for internal calculations, which can be more accurate but slower.

enabled.description: Enable periodic incremental backups. When enabled, full_backup_week_schedule must be set. Incremental backups only store changes since the last backup, making them faster and more storage-efficient than full backups. This is particularly useful for large databases where daily full backups would be too time-consuming or expensive.

full_backup_week_schedule.description: Comma-separated list of days of the week when full backups should be created. Valid values: mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat, sun. Default is null. Example : "mon,fri,sun".

auth_plugin.description:
A string specifying the authentication method to be used for connections
to the MySQL user account. The valid values are `mysql_native_password`
or `caching_sha2_password`. If excluded when creating a new user, the
default for the version of MySQL in use will be used. As of MySQL 8.0, the
default is `caching_sha2_password`.

indices_memory_index_buffer_size_percent.description: Total amount of heap used for indexing buffer before writing segments to disk, expressed as a percentage. Too low value will slow down indexing; too high value will increase indexing performance but causes performance issues for query performance.

indices_memory_max_index_buffer_size_mb.description: Maximum amount of heap used for indexing buffer before writing segments to disk, in mb. Works in conjunction with indices_memory_index_buffer_size_percentage, each being enforced. The default is unbounded.

indices_memory_min_index_buffer_size_mb.description: Minimum amount of heap used for indexing buffer before writing segments to disk, in mb. Works in conjunction with indices_memory_index_buffer_size_percentage, each being enforced.

indices_queries_cache_size_percentage.description: Maximum amount of heap used for query cache.  Too low value will decrease query performance and increase performance for other operations; too high value will cause issues with other functionality.

indices_query_bool_max_clause_count.description: Maximum number of clauses Lucene BooleanQuery can have.  Only increase it if necessary, as it may cause performance issues.

indices_recovery_max_concurrent_file_chu.description: Maximum number of file chunks sent in parallel for each recovery.

indices_recovery_max_mb_per_sec.description: Limits total inbound and outbound recovery traffic for each node, expressed in mb per second. Applies to both peer recoveries as well as snapshot recoveries (i.e., restores from a snapshot).

ism_enabled.description: Specifies whether ISM is enabled or not.

ism_history_enabled.description: Specifies whether audit history is enabled or not. The logs from ISM are automatically indexed to a logs document.

ism_history_max_age_hours.description: Maximum age before rolling over the audit history index, in hours.

ism_history_max_docs.description: Maximum number of documents before rolling over the audit history index.

ism_history_rollover_check_period_hours.description: The time between rollover checks for the audit history index, in hours.

ism_history_rollover_retention_period_da.description: Length of time long audit history indices are kept, in days.

keep_index_refresh_interval.description: DigitalOcean automatically resets the `index.refresh_interval` to the default value (once per second) to  ensure that new documents are quickly available for search queries. If you are setting your own refresh intervals,  you can disable this by setting this field to true.

knn_memory_circuit_breaker_enabled.description: Enable or disable KNN memory circuit breaker.

knn_memory_circuit_breaker_limit.description: Maximum amount of memory in percentage that can be used for the KNN index. Defaults to 50% of the JVM heap size.  0 is used to set it to null which can be used to invalidate caches.

override_main_response_version.description: Compatibility mode sets OpenSearch to report its version as 7.10 so clients continue to work.

plugins_alerting_filter_by_backend_roles.description: Enable or disable filtering of alerting by backend roles.

reindex_remote_whitelist.description: Allowlist of remote IP addresses for reindexing. Changing this value will cause all OpenSearch instances to restart.

script_max_compilations_rate.description: Limits the number of inline script compilations within a period of time. Default is use-context

search_max_buckets.description: Maximum number of aggregation buckets allowed in a single response.

thread_pool_analyze_queue_size.description: Size of queue for operations in the analyze thread pool.

thread_pool_analyze_size.description: Number of workers in the analyze operation thread pool.  Do note this may have maximum value depending on CPU count - value is automatically lowered if set to higher than maximum value.

thread_pool_force_merge_size.description: Number of workers in the force merge operation thread pool. This pool is used for forcing a merge between shards of one or more indices. Do note this may have maximum value depending on CPU count - value is automatically lowered if set to higher than maximum value.

thread_pool_get_queue_size.description: Size of queue for operations in the get thread pool.

thread_pool_get_size.description: Number of workers in the get operation thread pool.  Do note this may have maximum value depending on CPU count - value is automatically lowered if set to higher than maximum value.

thread_pool_search_queue_size.description: Size of queue for operations in the search thread pool.

thread_pool_search_size.description: Number of workers in the search operation thread pool.  Do note this may have maximum value depending on CPU count - value is automatically lowered if set to higher than maximum value.

thread_pool_search_throttled_queue_size.description: Size of queue for operations in the search throttled thread pool.

thread_pool_search_throttled_size.description: Number of workers in the search throttled operation thread pool. This pool is used for searching frozen indices. Do note this may have maximum value depending on CPU count - value is automatically lowered if set to higher than maximum value.

thread_pool_write_queue_size.description: Size of queue for operations in the write thread pool.

thread_pool_write_size.description: Number of workers in the write operation thread pool.  Do note this may have maximum value depending on CPU count - value is automatically lowered if set to higher than maximum value.

Each is a dotted path of up to 8 segments made of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, and must be declared by the tool's output schema; arrays are traversed element-wise. You can bind only the released version your catalog exposes: an unpinned slug resolves it and the response echoes it as version; a pin must equal it, and a `tool_id` (the opaque identity from tool search) must be that version. patch_session_request.description: PATCH body for /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}: an allowlisted subset of session-scoped settings (never environment-spec / config mutation). At least one property below must be present; {} is 400. Unknown top-level keys are rejected with 400. New patchable fields will be added here as optional properties over time.

resume_on_topoff.description: When present, sets whether this session opts in to automatic resumption when the team's prepayment balance is restored after a low-balance pause. Session-scoped consent, not config-scoped. Omitted properties are not modified.

pending_deployment_spec.description: Pending deployment when status is provisioning or updating.

enable_public_endpoint.description: Whether to expose a public LLM endpoint.

model_deployments.description: At least one model deployment is required.

name.description: Name of the Dedicated Inference. Must be unique within the team.

version.description: Spec version.

uuid.description: VPC UUID for the Dedicated Inference.

permission_filesystem.description: Filesystem boundary, enforced by the microVM (read-only root + bind-mounted writable roots) for every agent.

allowWrite.description: Additional writable paths beyond the workspace. Values must not contain shell-style ${VAR}/$VAR expansions.

permission_network.description: Network boundary. Narrows (subtract-only) spec.sandbox.egress; link-local/internal addresses stay blocked by the broader egress policy.

enforcement.description: What happens when the agent cannot enforce the rule exactly. "strict" rejects the session; "best-effort" degrades to the closest more-restrictive form and warns (never widens). Defaults to strict for deny rules, best-effort otherwise.

match.description: Optional keys narrowing the rule (e.g. {"command": "npm run deploy"} for bash). Values are globs and must not contain shell-style ${VAR}/$VAR expansions.

tool.description: Tool taxonomy this rule matches (e.g. bash, file.read, file.write, web.fetch, git.*, mcp).

permissions.description: Customer-declared tool-execution permission policy (spec.permissions). REQUEST only: the policy engine resolves it (∩ tenant ∩ platform) into the canonical policy and validates it against the (agent, version) capability descriptor. Absent or empty means the agent keeps its built-in default gating — no policy is shipped to the sandbox.

defaultAction.description: Disposition for tool calls that match no rule. Defaults to "ask" when omitted.

rules.description: Ordered match→action rules. Declared order is authoritative: the LAST matching rule wins (author-order last-match).

autodb_idle_timeout.description: If the automatically-created database pools have been unused this many seconds, they are freed. If 0, timeout is disabled.

autodb_max_db_connections.description: Only allows a maximum this many server connections per database (regardless of user). If 0, allows unlimited connections.

autodb_pool_size.description: If non-zero, automatically creates a pool of that size per user when a pool doesn't exist.

ignore_startup_parameters.description: List of parameters to ignore when given in startup packet.

items.description: Enum of parameters to ignore when given in startup packet.

min_pool_size.description: If current server connections are below this number, adds more. Improves behavior when usual load comes suddenly back after period of total inactivity. The value is effectively capped at the pool size.

server_idle_timeout.description: Drops server connections if they have been idle more than this many seconds.  If 0, timeout is disabled.

server_lifetime.description: The pooler closes any unused server connection that has been connected longer than this amount of seconds.

server_reset_query_always.description: Run server_reset_query (DISCARD ALL) in all pooling modes.

plan_downgrades.description: Resources moving to a tier at a given effective time.

effective_at.description: When the coverage downgrade takes effect.

resources.description: URNs of resources that will be downgraded.

autovacuum_analyze_scale_factor.description: Specifies a fraction, in a decimal value, of the table size to add to autovacuum_analyze_threshold when deciding whether to trigger an ANALYZE. The default is 0.2 (20% of table size).

autovacuum_analyze_threshold.description: Specifies the minimum number of inserted, updated, or deleted tuples needed to trigger an ANALYZE in any one table. The default is 50 tuples.

autovacuum_freeze_max_age.description: Specifies the maximum age (in transactions) that a table's pg_class.relfrozenxid field can attain before a VACUUM operation is forced to prevent transaction ID wraparound within the table. Note that the system will launch autovacuum processes to prevent wraparound even when autovacuum is otherwise disabled. This parameter will cause the server to be restarted.

autovacuum_max_workers.description: Specifies the maximum number of autovacuum processes (other than the autovacuum launcher) that may be running at any one time. The default is three. This parameter can only be set at server start.

autovacuum_naptime.description: Specifies the minimum delay, in seconds, between autovacuum runs on any given database. The default is one minute.

autovacuum_vacuum_cost_delay.description: Specifies the cost delay value, in milliseconds, that will be used in automatic VACUUM operations. If -1, uses the regular vacuum_cost_delay value, which is 20 milliseconds.

autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit.description: Specifies the cost limit value that will be used in automatic VACUUM operations. If -1 is specified (which is the default), the regular vacuum_cost_limit value will be used.

autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor.description: Specifies a fraction, in a decimal value, of the table size to add to autovacuum_vacuum_threshold when deciding whether to trigger a VACUUM. The default is 0.2 (20% of table size).

autovacuum_vacuum_threshold.description: Specifies the minimum number of updated or deleted tuples needed to trigger a VACUUM in any one table. The default is 50 tuples.

backup_hour.description: The hour of day (in UTC) when backup for the service starts. New backup only starts if previous backup has already completed.

backup_minute.description: The minute of the backup hour when backup for the service starts. New backup is only started if previous backup has already completed.

bgwriter_delay.description: Specifies the delay, in milliseconds, between activity rounds for the background writer. Default is 200 ms.

bgwriter_flush_after.description: The amount of kilobytes that need to be written by the background writer before attempting to force the OS to issue these writes to underlying storage. Specified in kilobytes, default is 512.  Setting of 0 disables forced writeback.

bgwriter_lru_maxpages.description: The maximum number of buffers that the background writer can write. Setting this to zero disables background writing. Default is 100.

bgwriter_lru_multiplier.description: The average recent need for new buffers is multiplied by bgwriter_lru_multiplier to arrive at an estimate of the number that will be needed during the next round, (up to bgwriter_lru_maxpages). 1.0 represents a “just in time” policy of writing exactly the number of buffers predicted to be needed. Larger values provide some cushion against spikes in demand, while smaller values intentionally leave writes to be done by server processes. The default is 2.0.

deadlock_timeout.description: The amount of time, in milliseconds, to wait on a lock before checking to see if there is a deadlock condition.

default_toast_compression.description: Specifies the default TOAST compression method for values of compressible columns (the default is lz4).

idle_in_transaction_session_timeout.description: Time out sessions with open transactions after this number of milliseconds

jit.description: Activates, in a boolean, the system-wide use of Just-in-Time Compilation (JIT).

log_autovacuum_min_duration.description: Causes each action executed by autovacuum to be logged if it ran for at least the specified number of milliseconds. Setting this to zero logs all autovacuum actions. Minus-one (the default) disables logging autovacuum actions.

log_error_verbosity.description: Controls the amount of detail written in the server log for each message that is logged.

log_line_prefix.description: Selects one of the available log-formats. These can support popular log analyzers like pgbadger, pganalyze, etc.

log_min_duration_statement.description: Log statements that take more than this number of milliseconds to run. If -1, disables.

max_connections.description: Sets the PostgreSQL maximum number of concurrent connections to the database server. This is a limited-release parameter. Contact your account team to confirm your eligibility. You cannot decrease this parameter value when set. For services with a read replica, first increase the read replica's value. After the change is applied to the replica, you can increase the primary service's value. Changing this parameter causes a service restart.

max_failover_replication_time_lag.description: Number of seconds of master unavailability before triggering database failover to standby. The default value is 60.

max_files_per_process.description: PostgreSQL maximum number of files that can be open per process.

max_locks_per_transaction.description: PostgreSQL maximum locks per transaction. Once increased, this parameter cannot be lowered from its set value.

max_logical_replication_workers.description: PostgreSQL maximum logical replication workers (taken from the pool of max_parallel_workers).

max_parallel_workers.description: Sets the maximum number of workers that the system can support for parallel queries.

max_parallel_workers_per_gather.description: Sets the maximum number of workers that can be started by a single Gather or Gather Merge node.

max_pred_locks_per_transaction.description: PostgreSQL maximum predicate locks per transaction.

max_prepared_transactions.description: PostgreSQL maximum prepared transactions. Once increased, this parameter cannot be lowered from its set value.

max_slot_wal_keep_size.description: PostgreSQL maximum WAL size (MB) reserved for replication slots. If -1 is specified, replication slots may retain an unlimited amount of WAL files. The default is -1 (upstream default). wal_keep_size minimum WAL size setting takes precedence over this.

max_stack_depth.description: Maximum depth of the stack in bytes.

max_standby_archive_delay.description: Max standby archive delay in milliseconds.

max_standby_streaming_delay.description: Max standby streaming delay in milliseconds.

max_wal_senders.description: PostgreSQL maximum WAL senders. Once increased, this parameter cannot be lowered from its set value.

max_worker_processes.description: Sets the maximum number of background processes that the system can support. Once increased, this parameter cannot be lowered from its set value.

pg_partman_bgw.interval.description: Sets the time interval to run pg_partman's scheduled tasks.

pg_partman_bgw.role.description: Controls which role to use for pg_partman's scheduled background tasks. Must consist of alpha-numeric characters, dots, underscores, or dashes. May not start with dash or dot. Maximum of 64 characters.

pg_stat_statements.track.description: Controls which statements are counted. Specify 'top' to track top-level statements (those issued directly by clients), 'all' to also track nested statements (such as statements invoked within functions), or 'none' to disable statement statistics collection. The default value is top.

pgaudit.description: System-wide settings for the pgaudit extension. When `feature_enabled` is true, the pgaudit extension is automatically installed. When false, the extension is uninstalled but auditing configurations (such as `log`) are preserved.

feature_enabled.description: Enable pgaudit extension. When enabled, pgaudit extension will be automatically installed. Otherwise, extension will be uninstalled but auditing configurations will be preserved.

log.description: Specifies which classes of statements will be logged by session audit logging. Available values are `read` (SELECT and COPY when the source is a relation or query), `write` (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, and COPY when the destination is a relation), `function` (function calls and DO blocks), `role` (statements related to roles and privileges: GRANT, REVOKE, CREATE/ALTER/DROP ROLE), `ddl` (all DDL that is not included in the role class), `misc` (miscellaneous commands, e.g. DISCARD, FETCH, CHECKPOINT, VACUUM, SET), `misc_set` (miscellaneous SET commands, e.g. SET ROLE), and `all` (include all of the above).

shared_buffers_percentage.description: Percentage of total RAM that the database server uses for shared memory buffers.  Valid range is 20-60 (float), which corresponds to 20% - 60%.  This setting adjusts the shared_buffers configuration value.

stat_monitor_enable.description: Enable the pg_stat_monitor extension. Enabling this extension will cause the cluster to be restarted. When this extension is enabled, pg_stat_statements results for utility commands are unreliable.

synchronous_replication.description: Synchronous replication type. Note that the service plan also needs to support synchronous replication.

temp_file_limit.description: PostgreSQL temporary file limit in KiB. If -1, sets to unlimited.

track_activity_query_size.description: Specifies the number of bytes reserved to track the currently executing command for each active session.

track_functions.description: Enables tracking of function call counts and time used.

track_io_timing.description: Enables timing of database I/O calls. This parameter is off by default, because it will repeatedly query the operating system for the current time, which may cause significant overhead on some platforms.

wal_sender_timeout.description: Terminate replication connections that are inactive for longer than this amount of time, in milliseconds. Setting this value to zero disables the timeout. Must be either 0 or between 5000 and 10800000.

wal_writer_delay.description: WAL flush interval in milliseconds. Note that setting this value to lower than the default 200ms may negatively impact performance

work_mem.description: The maximum amount of memory, in MB, used by a query operation (such as a sort or hash table) before writing to temporary disk files. Default is 1MB + 0.075% of total RAM (up to 32MB).

created_at.description: Time at which the prepayment configuration was created.

is_auto_prepay_enabled.description: Whether automatic prepayment top-up is enabled.

prepay_amount.description: Amount to charge when auto top-up triggers. Decimal dollars, e.g. `"50.00"`.

prepay_threshold.description: Balance threshold that triggers auto top-up. Decimal dollars, e.g. `"10.00"`.

spend_limit.description: Maximum spend allowed before the prepayment gate blocks usage. Decimal dollars, e.g. `"100.00"`.

updated_at.description: Time at which the prepayment configuration was last updated.

balance.description: Current prepayment balance. Decimal dollars, e.g. `"25.00"`.

blocked.description: Whether the prepayment gate is currently blocking usage.

eligible.description: Whether the account is eligible for the prepayment gate experience.

is_auto_prepay_enabled.description: Whether automatic prepayment top-up is enabled.

month_to_date_balance.description: Current account balance including month-to-date usage. Decimal dollars, e.g. `"75.00"`.

count.description: Number of times the charge was applied

name.description: Description of the charge

items.description: List of amount, and grouped aggregates by resource type.

name.description: Description of usage charges

is_default.description: If true, all resources will be added to this project if no project is specified.

resources.description: A list of uniform resource names (URNs) to be added to a project. Only resources that you are authorized to see will be returned.

created_at.description: A time value given in ISO8601 combined date and time format that represents when the project was created.

description.description: The description of the project. The maximum length is 255 characters.

environment.description: The environment of the project's resources.

id.description: The unique universal identifier of this project.

name.description: The human-readable name for the project. The maximum length is 175 characters and the name must be unique.

owner_id.description: The integer id of the project owner.

owner_uuid.description: The unique universal identifier of the project owner.

purpose.description:
The purpose of the project. The maximum length is 255 characters. It can
have one of the following values:

- Just trying out DigitalOcean
- Class project / Educational purposes
- Website or blog
- Web Application
- Service or API
- Mobile Application
- Machine learning / AI / Data processing
- IoT
- Operational / Developer tooling

If another value for purpose is specified, for example, "your custom purpose",
your purpose will be stored as `Other: your custom purpose`.

updated_at.description: A time value given in ISO8601 combined date and time format that represents when the project was updated.

result.description: One entry per matching series, each carrying the samples evaluated at every step across the requested range.

prom_metric_labels.description: Metric labels as key/value pairs. By default, metric names in responses use Prometheus underscored spelling (for example `do_droplets_cpu_time`), even when the request used a dotted selector (for example `do.droplets.cpu_time`).

result.description: Result payload shape depends on `resultType`. `vector` and `matrix` are series arrays. `scalar` and `string` both use a `[timestamp, value]` sample pair.

prom_sample.description: A Prometheus sample as `[timestamp_seconds, value]`. The timestamp is a UNIX epoch float; the value is a string.

provider_health.description: Health of one provider, combining its tools.

provider_summary.description: Describes a catalog provider and how to authenticate to it.

auth_type.description: Deprecated: read `auth_types`, since a provider may accept more than one credential kind. This is the first entry of `auth_types` other than `none`, or `none` when that is the only entry.

auth_types.description:
Credential kinds the provider accepts, sorted:
none|oauth|`shared_api_key`|unknown|`user_oauth_app`|`user_token`.

`none` means the provider needs no credential. `oauth` means users can connect through
DigitalOcean's shared OAuth application. `user_oauth_app` means users can connect through an OAuth
client your team registers as a provider credential; without `oauth` alongside it, that is the only
way to connect. `shared_api_key` means DigitalOcean supplies the key. `user_token` means your team
or its users supply a key or token.

`unknown` means the provider declares no kind this API recognizes, including an OAuth provider whose
shared application is not available. It is never paired with another kind.

connection_parameters.description: Non-sensitive values collected when creating a connection. Set only when `auth_types` contains `oauth` or `user_oauth_app`.

credential_parameters.description: Non-secret values collected when registering an API key provider credential. They are validated against the provider's declaration and used to derive the credential's `base_url`; callers cannot supply header names or arbitrary destinations.

name.description: Provider slug, used as provider when creating a connection or a provider credential.

oauth_client_setup_url.description: HTTPS page at the provider where a team creates that OAuth client, such as its developer console or setup guide. Empty unless `auth_types` contains `user_oauth_app` and the provider declares one.

oauth_redirect_url.description: Callback URL a team must register with the provider when it creates its own OAuth client. It is the same for every provider and cannot be changed per credential. Empty unless `auth_types` contains `user_oauth_app`.

scopes.description: The OAuth scopes a connection may request; a connection that requests none gets all of them. Set only when `auth_types` contains `oauth` or `user_oauth_app`.

redis_maxmemory_policy.description:
A string specifying the desired eviction policy for the Caching cluster.

- `noeviction`: Don't evict any data, returns error when memory limit is reached.
- `allkeys-lru:` Evict any key, least recently used (LRU) first.
- `allkeys-random`: Evict keys in a random order.
- `volatile-lru`: Evict keys with expiration only, least recently used (LRU) first.
- `volatile-random`: Evict keys with expiration only in a random order.
- `volatile-ttl`: Evict keys with expiration only, shortest time-to-live (TTL) first.

redis_notify_keyspace_events.description:
Set notify-keyspace-events option. Requires at least `K` or `E` and accepts any combination of the following options. Setting the parameter to `""` disables notifications.
- `K` — Keyspace events
- `E` — Keyevent events
- `g` — Generic commands (e.g. `DEL`, `EXPIRE`, `RENAME`, ...)
- `$` — String commands
- `l` — List commands
- `s` — Set commands
- `h` — Hash commands
- `z` — Sorted set commands
- `t` — Stream commands
- `d` — Module key type events
- `x` — Expired events
- `e` — Evicted events
- `m` — Key miss events
- `n` — New key events
- `A` — Alias for `"g$lshztxed"`

redis_persistence.description: Creates an RDB dump of the database every 10 minutes that can be used  to recover data after a node crash. The database does not create the  dump if no keys have changed since the last dump. When set to `off`,  the database cannot fork services, and data can be lost if a service  is restarted or powered off. DigitalOcean Managed Caching databases  do not support the Append Only File (AOF) persistence method.

- When enabled, Caching accepts only SSL connections on port `25061`.
- When disabled, port `25060` is opened for non-SSL connections, while port `25061` remains available for SSL connections.

logline.description:
Conditional (required if `format` == `custom`).

Syslog log line template for a custom format, supporting limited rsyslog style templating (using `%tag%`). Supported tags are: `HOSTNAME`, `app-name`, `msg`, `msgid`, `pri`, `procid`, `structured-data`, `timestamp` and `timestamp:::date-rfc3339`.

---
**Datadog Integration Example for Non-Mongo clusters**:
```
DD_KEY <%pri%>1 %timestamp:::date-rfc3339% %HOSTNAME%.DB_NAME %app-name% - - - %msg%
```
- Replace `DD_KEY` with your actual Datadog API key.
- Replace `DB_NAME` with the actual name of your database cluster.
- Configure the Server:
  - US Region: Use `intake.logs.datadoghq.com`
  - EU Region: Use `tcp-intake.logs.datadoghq.eu`
- Configure the Port:
  - US Region: Use port `10516`
  - EU Region: Use port `443`
- Enable TLS:
  - Ensure the TLS checkbox is enabled.
- Note: This configuration applies to **non-Mongo clusters only**. For **Mongo clusters**, use the `datadog_logsink` integration instead.

tags.description:
A tag is a label that can be applied to a resource (currently Droplets, Images, Volumes, Volume Snapshots, and Database clusters) in order to better organize or facilitate the lookups and actions on it.
Tags have two attributes: a user defined `name` attribute and an embedded `resources` attribute with information about resources that have been tagged.

name.description:
The name of the tag. Tags may contain letters, numbers, colons, dashes, and underscores.
There is a limit of 255 characters per tag.

**Note:** Tag names are case stable, which means the capitalization you use when you first create a tag is canonical.

When working with tags in the API, you must use the tag's canonical capitalization. For example, if you create a tag named "PROD", the URL to add that tag to a resource would be `https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/tags/PROD/resources` (not `/v2/tags/prod/resources`).

Tagged resources in the control panel will always display the canonical capitalization. For example, if you create a tag named "PROD", you can tag resources in the control panel by entering "prod". The tag will still display with its canonical capitalization, "PROD".

allOf.description:
Databases that are tagged with the specified tag.
Requires `database:read` scope.

Droplets that are tagged with the specified tag.
Requires `droplet:read` scope.

Images that are tagged with the specified tag.
Requires `image:read` scope.

Volume Snapshots that are tagged with the specified tag.
Requires `block_storage_snapshot:read` scope.

Volumes that are tagged with the specified tag.
Requires `block_storage:read` scope.

resources.description:
An embedded object containing key value pairs of resource type and resource statistics.
It also includes a count of the total number of resources tagged with the current tag as well as a `last_tagged_uri` attribute set to the last resource tagged with the current tag.

This will only include resources that you are authorized to see. For example, to see tagged Droplets, include the `droplet:read` scope.

tags_array.description:
A flat array of tag names as strings to be applied to the resource. Tag names may be for either existing or new tags.

Requires `tag:create` scope.

tags_array_read.description:
A flat array of tag names as strings applied to the resource.

Requires `tag:read` scope.

An array of objects containing resource_id and resource_type 
attributes.

This response will only include resources that you are authorized to see.
For example, to see Droplets, include the `droplet:read` scope.

traces_field_ref.description: A reference to a span field, used in filters and `order_by`.

name.description:
The field name. Without `scope`, these names (case-insensitive) resolve to built-in span columns: `trace_id`, `span_id`, `parent_span_id`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `duration_ns`, `name` (`span.name`), `kind` (`span.kind`), `status_code` (`status.code`, `status_code`), `status_message`, and `service_name` (`service.name`). Any other name is looked up as a span attribute, falling back to a resource attribute. With `scope` set, `name` is always treated as an attribute key. Attribute keys may contain only letters, digits, and `.`, `_`, `-`, `/`, `:`, `@`.

In traces `order_by`, `name` must be a trace-level sort field instead; see the `order_by` field description.

scope.description: Restricts the lookup to one attribute map and is matched case-insensitively. `FIELD_SCOPE_RESOURCE` reads resource attributes and accepts `resource` or `resource.attributes` as aliases. `FIELD_SCOPE_ATTRIBUTES` reads span attributes and accepts `attribute`, `attributes`, or `span.attributes` as aliases. Omit to use the built-in column mapping described for `name`. Ignored in traces `order_by`.

traces_filter_condition.description: A single field comparison in a traces filter expression.

traces_filter_expression.description: A boolean filter tree for traces queries. Exactly one node is set per message. Trees may be nested at most 16 levels deep and contain at most 256 nodes in total.

text_search.description: A substring search across span names, service names, and status messages.

query.description: The search string. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed, and the remaining string must not be empty.

traces_filter_value.description: A typed literal or list value for a traces filter condition. Exactly one kind is set per message.

traces_order_by.description:
A sort clause for traces search results. Supported `field.name` values are `started`, `duration_ns`, `service_name`, `trace_id`, `error_count`, `span_count`, and `status`. Any other name returns `400`.

Sorting by `started` is exact. For every other field, the server first selects the most recent matching traces by start time (up to the requested limit) and then sorts only those traces, so results are not a global top-N across the whole time range.

direction.description: The sort direction, matched case-insensitively. Omit to use the server default.

traces_pagination_request.description: Limits the size of a traces search result set. There is no cursor; use `pagination.has_more` in the response to tell whether more traces matched, and narrow the time range or filter to see them.

limit.description: Maximum number of traces to return. Omitted or `0` uses the default of 100. Negative values or values above 1000 return `400`; they are not clamped.

has_more.description: Whether more results matched the query than were returned.

traces_search_request.description: Request body for searching traces. Unknown properties are rejected.

order_by.description: Sort clauses applied in order. Defaults to `started` descending.

traces_search_response.description: Response body for a traces search.

data.description: Matching traces. Empty when no traces match.

name.description: The span name, typically the operation being performed.

resource.description: Resource attributes associated with the span.

service_name.description: The service that emitted the span. Omitted when the span has no service.name resource attribute.

status_code.description: The OpenTelemetry span status code as a string: `Unset`, `Ok`, or `Error`.

status_message.description: The status description. Omitted when empty.

trace_id.description: The trace this span belongs to.

traces_time_instant.description: A single point in time. Set `absolute` or `relative`; if both are set, `absolute` is used.

absolute.description: An absolute timestamp, either RFC3339 (with optional fractional seconds) or a Unix epoch integer as a decimal string. Epoch precision is inferred from magnitude: seconds, milliseconds, microseconds, or nanoseconds.

relative.description: A time relative to now. Use `now` for the current time, a bare duration such as `15m` or `24h` to look back from now, or an offset such as `now-2h` or `now+30m`. Supported units are `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`, and `w`; decimal amounts such as `1.5h` are allowed.

traces_time_range.description: An inclusive query time window. Both bounds are required, `from` must not be after `to`, and the window must not exceed 7 days (`168h`).

traces_trace_response.description: A single trace and all of its spans.

spans.description: Every span in the trace, ordered by start time.

truncated.description: True when the trace has more spans than were returned in this response. Omitted when false.

traces_trace_summary.description: A single trace returned by a traces search. One row per trace, aggregated from its spans. Every field except `trace_id` is omitted when it holds its zero value (for example, `error_count` is absent when no spans errored).

duration_ns.description: Wall-clock duration of the trace in nanoseconds.

error_count.description: The number of spans in the trace with an `Error` status code. Omitted when zero.

service_name.description: The service that emitted the root span. Omitted when the root span has no service.name resource attribute.

span_count.description: The number of spans in the trace.

span_names.description: The distinct span names present in the trace.

started.description: The start time of the earliest span in the trace, in RFC 3339 format.

status.description: The rolled-up status of the trace. `Error` if any span has an `Error` status code, otherwise `Ok`.

transfer_id.description: A unique number that used to identify and reference an image account transfer.

trigger.description: A single automation bound to exactly one agent/session (agent == session in v1). The nested block present depends on `kind` (webhook xor cron) and `session_mode` (fresh => session_template; reuse => bound_session_id). `agent_kind` is read-only and derived; the webhook secret, the output email address / Slack webhook URL, and any env values inside session_template are write-only and never returned.

bound_session_id.description: Present iff session_mode=reuse. UUID of the existing PAUSED session this trigger resumes; may be shared by multiple triggers.

name.description: Unique per team among non-deleted triggers. Same rules as session names; not UUID-form.

prompt_template.description: The prompt sent on each fire. Opaque to clients; payload-interpolation syntax is server-defined. For cron triggers it must not reference payload placeholders.
prompt_template.example: Review the latest push and summarize risks.

session_template.description: Present iff session_mode=fresh. The agents.yaml Agent manifest used to CREATE a session on each fire, returned with its env values REDACTED.

trigger_execution.description: One row per firing (webhook delivery or cron tick).

failure_reason.description: Client-safe reason when status=failed; absent otherwise. One of a fixed set of messages; do not parse it or match on substrings. Quote the execution_id when contacting support.

output_text.description: The doctl-parity transcript rendered from the run's SPI events. Returned by GetTriggerExecution only; omitted from list items.

output_truncated.description: True when output_text is incomplete. Returned by GetTriggerExecution only; omitted from list items.

payload.description: The raw webhook body or cron tick metadata. Returned by GetTriggerExecution only; omitted from list items. Cleared for terminal executions after the payload retention window (default 7 days from creation).

run_id.description: Populated once SendInput acks; correlation/audit only. May be empty.

session_id.description: The run's session. Populated once the session is created (fresh) or is known (reuse); empty before then.

created_at.description: UTC time string.

function.description: Name of function(action) that exists in the given namespace.

is_enabled.description: Indicates weather the trigger is paused or unpaused.

name.description: The trigger's unique name within the namespace.

namespace.description: A unique string format of UUID with a prefix fn-.

last_run_at.description: Indicates last run time. null value indicates trigger not run yet.

next_run_at.description: Indicates next run time. null value indicates trigger will not run.

type.description: String which indicates the type of trigger source like SCHEDULED.

updated_at.description: UTC time string.

trigger_kind.description: How the trigger fires - on an event (webhook) or on a schedule (cron). Immutable after create.

trigger_output_mode.description: none = nothing pushed; the result stays in run history for self-serve. email = the collected run output is emailed to a configured address. slack = the collected run output is posted to a Slack incoming webhook URL (channel fixed by the webhook at install time).

trigger_output_read.description: Output-delivery configuration as seen on reads. The email address and Slack webhook URL are write-only and never returned.

email_configured.description: True when an email address is stored (mode=email).

slack_configured.description: True when a Slack incoming webhook URL is stored (mode=slack).

trigger_output_write.description: Output-delivery configuration on create/update. Exactly one of email / slack is required for the matching mode and forbidden otherwise; destinations are stored encrypted and never returned.

trigger_session_mode.description: fresh = a new session is created from the trigger's spec on every firing and destroyed after. reuse = the trigger binds an existing PAUSED session, resumed on each firing and paused after; multiple triggers may bind one session.

trigger_status.description: Trigger lifecycle state. Soft-deleted triggers are never returned (404).

certificate_id.description: The ID of a DigitalOcean managed TLS certificate used for SSL when a custom subdomain is provided.

custom_domain.description: The fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of the custom subdomain used with the CDN endpoint.

ttl.description: The amount of time the content is cached by the CDN's edge servers in seconds. TTL must be one of 60, 600, 3600, 86400, or 604800. Defaults to 3600 (one hour) when excluded.

cancel.description: A boolean value indicating that the garbage collection should be cancelled.

is_enabled.description: Indicates weather the trigger is paused or unpaused.

update_trigger_request.description: Partial update. Only the supplied fields change. kind and webhook.provider are immutable. Sending status alone is how pause/re-enable work.

bound_session_id.description: reuse triggers only. UUID of an existing session owned by the team.

name.description: New team-unique trigger name. Same charset/length rules as create.

prompt_template.example: Review the latest push and summarize risks.

session_template.description: fresh triggers only. A session_template PATCH is a full replacement of the stored template; you must resupply every spec.secrets slot value the new manifest declares, or the request is a 400.

acl.description: ACLs (Access Control Lists) specifying permissions on topics within a Kafka cluster.

id.description: An identifier for the ACL. Will be computed after the ACL is created/updated.

permission.description: Permission set applied to the ACL. 'consume' allows for messages to be consumed from the topic. 'produce' allows for messages to be published to the topic. 'produceconsume' allows for both 'consume' and 'produce' permission. 'admin' allows for 'produceconsume' as well as any operations to administer the topic (delete, update).

mongo_user_settings.description: MongoDB-specific settings for the user. Configure these when creating a user. Updating MongoDB roles or database access after creation is not supported; recreate the user to change them. This option is not currently supported for other database engines.

databases.description: A list of databases to which the user should have access. When the database is set to `admin`, the user will have access to all databases based on the user's role i.e. a user with the role `readOnly` assigned to the `admin` database will have read access to all databases.

role.description: The role to assign to the user with each role mapping to a MongoDB built-in role.  `readOnly` maps to a [read](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/built-in-roles/#mongodb-authrole-read) role. `readWrite` maps to a [readWrite](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/built-in-roles/#mongodb-authrole-readWrite) role. `dbAdmin` maps to a [dbAdmin](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/built-in-roles/#mongodb-authrole-dbAdmin) role.

index.description: A regex for matching the indexes that this ACL should apply to.

permission.description: Permission set applied to the ACL. 'read' allows user to read from the index. 'write' allows for user to write to the index. 'readwrite' allows for both 'read' and 'write' permission. 'deny'(default) restricts user from performing any operation over an index. 'admin' allows for 'readwrite' as well as any operations to administer the index.

privileges. When omitted on create or update, the value defaults to
`false` and replication privileges are not granted. This option is not
currently supported for other database engines.

User settings that can be updated via the Update a Database User endpoint.
Supported for PostgreSQL, Kafka, and OpenSearch clusters. For other engines,
the request returns a 422. MongoDB user roles and database access
(`mongo_user_settings`) cannot be updated after creation; recreate the user
to change them.

name.description: A globally unique name for the container registry. Must be lowercase and be composed only of numbers, letters and `-`, up to a limit of 63 characters.

validation_result.description: Response of POST /v2/agents/sessions/policy/validate: per-rule verdicts for the (agent, version). The same shape is persisted per session in session_policies.verdicts.

defaultAction.description: Catch-all disposition AS SHIPPED (after unverified allow→ask downgrade). When defaultActionVerdict is degraded, this remains the shipped value; see defaultActionRendered for what the agent will actually enforce.

defaultActionReason.description: Human-readable explanation when defaultActionVerdict is degraded.

defaultActionRendered.description: Disposition the agent will actually enforce as the catch-all: equals defaultAction when exact; the more-restrictive degrade target (usually ask) when degraded.

defaultActionVerdict.description: exact — agent can enforce the catch-all as written; degraded — agent cannot enforce the requested defaultAction (warn-only; shipped value unchanged); omitted when no descriptor was available to classify against.

ok.description: False when any strict rule is unsupported or unverified — i.e. CreateSession would reject this policy for this (agent, version).

frequent_snapshots.description:
Frequent RDB snapshots
When enabled, Valkey will create frequent local RDB snapshots. When disabled, Valkey will only take RDB snapshots when a backup is created, based on the backup schedule. This setting is ignored when valkey_persistence is set to off.

valkey_acl_channels_default.description: Determines default pub/sub channels' ACL for new users if ACL is not supplied. When this option is not defined, all_channels is assumed to keep backward compatibility. This option doesn't affect Valkey configuration acl-pubsub-default.

valkey_active_expire_effort.description:
Active expire effort
Valkey reclaims expired keys both when accessed and in the background. The background process scans for expired keys to free memory. Increasing the active-expire-effort setting (default 1, max 10) uses more CPU to reclaim expired keys faster, reducing memory usage but potentially increasing latency.

valkey_lfu_decay_time.description: LFU maxmemory-policy counter decay time in minutes

valkey_lfu_log_factor.description: Counter logarithm factor for volatile-lfu and allkeys-lfu maxmemory-policies

valkey_notify_keyspace_events.description:
Set notify-keyspace-events option. Requires at least `K` or `E` and accepts any combination of the following options. Setting the parameter to `""` disables notifications.
- `K` — Keyspace events
- `E` — Keyevent events
- `g` — Generic commands (e.g. `DEL`, `EXPIRE`, `RENAME`, ...)
- `$` — String commands
- `l` — List commands
- `s` — Set commands
- `h` — Hash commands
- `z` — Sorted set commands
- `t` — Stream commands
- `d` — Module key type events
- `x` — Expired events
- `e` — Evicted events
- `m` — Key miss events
- `n` — New key events
- `A` — Alias for `"g$lshztxed"`

valkey_number_of_databases.description: Set number of valkey databases. Changing this will cause a restart of valkey service.

valkey_persistence.description: When persistence is 'rdb', Valkey does RDB dumps each 10 minutes if any key is changed. Also RDB dumps are done according to backup schedule for backup purposes. When persistence is 'off', no RDB dumps and backups are done, so data can be lost at any moment if service is restarted for any reason, or if service is powered off. Also service can't be forked.

valkey_pubsub_client_output_buffer_limit.description: Set output buffer limit for pub / sub clients in MB. The value is the hard limit, the soft limit is 1/4 of the hard limit. When setting the limit, be mindful of the available memory in the selected service plan.

valkey_timeout.description: Valkey idle connection timeout in seconds

bearer_auth.description:
## OAuth Authentication

In order to interact with the DigitalOcean API, you or your application must
authenticate.

The DigitalOcean API handles this through OAuth, an open standard for
authorization. OAuth allows you to delegate access to your account.
Scopes can be used to grant full access, read-only access, or access to
a specific set of endpoints.

You can generate an OAuth token by visiting the [Apps & API](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/api/tokens)
section of the DigitalOcean control panel for your account.

An OAuth token functions as a complete authentication request. In effect, it
acts as a substitute for a username and password pair.

Because of this, it is absolutely **essential** that you keep your OAuth
tokens secure. In fact, upon generation, the web interface will only display
each token a single time in order to prevent the token from being compromised.

DigitalOcean access tokens begin with an identifiable prefix in order to
distinguish them from other similar tokens.

- `dop_v1_` for personal access tokens generated in the control panel
- `doo_v1_` for tokens generated by applications using [the OAuth flow](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/oauth-api/)
- `dor_v1_` for OAuth refresh tokens

### Scopes

Scopes act like permissions assigned to an API token. These permissions
determine what actions the token can perform. You can create API
tokens that grant read-only access, full access, or limited access to
specific endpoints by using custom scopes.

Generally, scopes are designed to match HTTP verbs and common CRUD
operations (Create, Read, Update, Delete).

| HTTP Verb | CRUD Operation | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| GET | Read | `<resource>:read` |
| POST | Create | `<resource>:create` |
| PUT/PATCH | Update | `<resource>:update` |
| DELETE | Delete | `<resource>:delete` |

For example, creating a new Droplet by making a `POST` request to the
`/v2/droplets` endpoint requires the `droplet:create` scope while
listing Droplets by making a `GET` request to the `/v2/droplets`
endpoint requires the `droplet:read` scope.

Each endpoint below specifies which scope is required to access it when
using custom scopes.

### How to Authenticate with OAuth

In order to make an authenticated request, include a bearer-type
`Authorization` header containing your OAuth token. All requests must be
made over HTTPS.

### Authenticate with a Bearer Authorization Header

```
curl -X $HTTP_METHOD -H "Authorization: Bearer $DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN" "https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/$OBJECT"
```

authenticate.

The DigitalOcean API handles this through OAuth, an open standard for
authorization. OAuth allows you to delegate access to your account.
Scopes can be used to grant full access, read-only access, or access to
a specific set of endpoints.

You can generate an OAuth token by visiting the [Apps & API](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/api/tokens)
section of the DigitalOcean control panel for your account.

An OAuth token functions as a complete authentication request. In effect, it
acts as a substitute for a username and password pair.

Because of this, it is absolutely **essential** that you keep your OAuth
tokens secure. In fact, upon generation, the web interface will only display
each token a single time in order to prevent the token from being compromised.

DigitalOcean access tokens begin with an identifiable prefix in order to
distinguish them from other similar tokens.

- `dop_v1_` for personal access tokens generated in the control panel
- `doo_v1_` for tokens generated by applications using [the OAuth flow](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/oauth-api/)
- `dor_v1_` for OAuth refresh tokens

### Authenticate with a Bearer Authorization Header

**Serverless Inference:**

```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN" "https://inference.do-ai.run/v1/chat/completions"
```

**Agent Inference:**

```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENT_ACCESS_KEY" "https://{your-agent-url}.agents.do-ai.run/v1/chat/completions?agent=true"
```

key) instead of a DigitalOcean OAuth token. The `agent_access_key` is
provided when you provision an agent endpoint and is scoped to that
specific agent. It is not interchangeable with DigitalOcean OAuth tokens
(`dop_v1_*`, `doo_v1_*`, `dor_v1_*`), which are used with Serverless
Inference and the control-plane API at `https://api.digitalocean.com`.

put.description:
Uploads the raw JSONL bytes to the presigned `upload_url` returned by `POST /v1/batches/files`.

**The URL is dynamic — do not construct it.** Use the `upload_url` value from the previous step verbatim. Its host, path, and query parameters are part of the short-lived (~15 minute) signature and change per request; the server and path shown here are illustrative. If the URL expires before the upload completes, create a new file intent and retry.

`POST /v1/batches` performs a `HEAD` check on the uploaded object and will reject the batch if this upload has not completed.

Send the raw JSONL bytes verbatim. Presigned PUT URLs are signature-sensitive to request headers — prefer `application/octet-stream` or omit `Content-Type` entirely. A custom value (for example `application/jsonl`) can cause signature mismatches unless the URL was signed for that exact header.

requestBody.description: Raw JSONL bytes — one request per line.

403.description: Signature mismatch or URL expired. Create a new file intent with `POST /v1/batches/files` and upload again.

servers.description: Use the exact `upload_url` returned by `POST /v1/batches/files`. Do not construct this URL — it is presigned, short-lived, and different per request.

put.summary: Upload a Batch Inference Input File

x-codeSamples.source:
# UPLOAD_URL is the exact upload_url returned by POST /v1/batches/files.
# Use it verbatim; do not modify the host, path, or query string.
#
# Send the raw JSONL bytes with --data-binary so line endings and UTF-8
# are preserved. The presigned URL is signature-sensitive: prefer
# application/octet-stream (or omit Content-Type entirely) — a custom
# value such as application/jsonl can break signature matching unless
# the URL was signed for that exact header.
curl -X PUT "$UPLOAD_URL" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \
  --data-binary "@batch_requests.jsonl"

# Two-step upload flow:
#   1. Reserve a file_id + presigned upload_url via client.batches.files.create.
#   2. PUT the raw JSONL bytes to upload_url.
#
# The presigned URL is short-lived (~15 minutes) and signature-sensitive —
# use it verbatim and prefer Content-Type application/octet-stream (or
# omit the header entirely). A custom value such as application/jsonl
# can break signature matching.
import os
from pathlib import Path

import requests
from pydo import Client

client = Client(token=os.environ.get("DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN"))

input_path = Path("batch_requests.jsonl")

# Step 1: reserve the upload slot.
intent = client.batches.files.create(file_name=input_path.name)
upload_url = intent["upload_url"]
file_id = intent["file_id"]

# Step 2: PUT the JSONL bytes to the presigned URL.
with input_path.open("rb") as fh:
    put = requests.put(
        upload_url,
        data=fh,
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/octet-stream"},
        timeout=60,
    )
put.raise_for_status()

print("uploaded file_id:", file_id)

post.description:
Approves or denies a tool call that is waiting for approval. A tool result returns `_meta.status` set to `requires_approval` when the session policy sets `ask` for the call, and its `_meta.decide` gives this request's path.

Send the decision with the session owner's token. Approval is a separate control request, not a tool, so an agent cannot approve its own calls. After approving, repeat the original call with the same arguments before `expires_at`. An approval applies only to that session, tool version, and set of arguments, and is used once. To ask again after a denial or expiry, repeat the tool call.

x-codeSamples.source:
curl -X POST \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"decision":"approve"}' \
  "https://actions.do-ai.run/approvals/session/$SESSION_ID/$APPROVAL_ID"

post.description: Approves or denies a tool call that is waiting for approval, identifying the session with the `X-Session-Id` header. It behaves the same as `POST /approvals/session/{session_id}/{approval_id}`, which is the path returned in a result's `_meta.decide`.

post.description:
Runs Python code in an ephemeral sandbox and returns its `stdout`, `stderr`, and `exit_code`. This is the REST form of the `action_code` MCP tool. Use it for computation, parsing, and data processing, or to chain several catalog tools in one request.

The sandbox provides `invoke_digitalocean_tool(name, arguments)`, which calls a catalog tool and returns a tool result. Those calls follow the session's tool selection and policy. Each request runs in a fresh sandbox, so state is not kept between requests. Execution, including tool calls, is time limited. Code that runs too long fails with a `timeout` error.

A nonzero exit code is still a `succeeded` result; check `output.exit_code`. If the session policy requires approval for `action_code`, the response is a failed result with `_meta.status` set to `requires_approval`.

200.description: The code ran, or it is waiting for approval. Check `status` before reading `output`.

  -H "X-Session-Id: $SESSION_ID" \
  -d '{"code":"print(\"hello from Action Gateway\")"}' \
  "https://actions.do-ai.run/code/execute"

post.description:
Runs 1 to 10 tool calls in parallel and returns one result per call, in request order. This is the REST form of the `action_invoke` MCP tool.

Each call is checked against the session's tool selection and policy, uses the session actor's connections, and applies any output view bound to the tool in the session. A well-formed request returns `200` even when some calls fail. Check each item's `result.status`, and use `success_count` and `error_count` to branch without scanning every item.

A call whose policy requires approval fails with `_meta.status` set to `requires_approval`. Have the session's owner approve it, then repeat the call with the same arguments. A call that needs the end user to connect a provider fails with `_meta.status` set to `requires_authorization` or `requires_connection_configuration`.

Each query is searched independently and returns its own result group, so you can see which tools serve which goal.
